characters.name: Tony Stark / Iron Man
characters.description: Genius billionaire weapons inventor who builds himself a high-tech suit of armor and kicks off the age of heroes.

phases.phase-1:
Iron Man: kidnapped in Afghanistan by men using his own weapons, he builds a suit in the cave to get out, comes home, shuts down Stark Industries' weapons division, and tells a press conference he is Iron Man rather than read the cover story.
The Incredible Hulk: one scene at the end, walking into a bar to tell General Ross that a team is being put together.
Iron Man 2: dying of palladium poisoning from the reactor in his chest while fending off the government and Ivan Vanko, until his father's old research points him at a new element.
The Avengers: he carries a nuclear missile through the wormhole over New York and very nearly does not come back.
phases.phase-2:
Iron Man 3: panic attacks after New York, and an armoury of suits he cannot stop building. The Mandarin turns out to be an actor fronting for Aldrich Killian and the Extremis programme. Tony ends the film by destroying the suits and having the shrapnel taken out of his chest.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: he and Bruce Banner build an artificial intelligence out of the Mind Stone without telling the others, and Ultron costs the world Sokovia. The treaty everyone argues about afterwards is named after that city.
phases.phase-3:
Captain America: Civil War: guilt over Sokovia makes him the loudest voice for the Accords, and it turns personal when he finds out the Winter Soldier killed his parents. He recruits Peter Parker on the way to that fight.
Spider-Man: Homecoming: he mentors Peter at arm's length and takes the suit back when Peter is not ready for it.
Avengers: Infinity War: stranded on Titan, stabbed with his own weapon, holding Peter while he turns to dust.
Avengers: Endgame: five years on he solves time travel at his kitchen table, runs the heist, and takes the Stones off Thanos to snap the army out of existence. It kills him.

characters.name: Steve Rogers / Captain America
characters.description: A scrawny kid from Brooklyn turned WWII super-soldier; the moral backbone of the Avengers.

phases.phase-1:
Captain America: The First Avenger: a ninety-pound volunteer from Brooklyn, and the only success Project Rebirth ever has. He loses Bucky off a moving train, puts the Red Skull's bomber into the Arctic to keep it off New York, and wakes up nearly seventy years later with everyone he knew gone.
The Avengers: Fury puts him back in uniform, and he ends up commanding the Battle of New York from street level.
phases.phase-2:
Captain America: The Winter Soldier: S.H.I.E.L.D. has been HYDRA from the inside since the 1940s, and the assassin sent to kill him is Bucky, kept frozen between jobs and used for seventy years. Steve brings the whole agency down rather than let Project Insight launch.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: by the end of it he is running a new Avengers roster out of the upstate compound.
phases.phase-3:
Ant-Man: the mid-credits only, on the other end of the scene where Sam finds something they cannot get to on their own.
Captain America: Civil War: he refuses the Accords, and when it comes down to the shield or Bucky he leaves the shield on the floor and spends two years underground.
Spider-Man: Homecoming: a set of school PSAs recorded long before any of that, still playing in the gym.
Avengers: Infinity War: back for Wakanda, which falls, and the Snap happens on his watch.
Avengers: Endgame: he runs the time heist, lifts Mjolnir against Thanos, and then stays in the past to have his dance with Peggy. He comes back old, and gives the shield to Sam Wilson.

characters.name: Thor
characters.description: The Asgardian God of Thunder, heir to the throne, armed with the enchanted hammer Mjolnir.

phases.phase-1:
Thor: banished to New Mexico without his powers for restarting a war he had been told to leave alone. He meets Jane Foster, earns Mjolnir back, and breaks the Bifrost to stop Loki wiping out Jotunheim.
The Avengers: he comes to Earth to take his brother home and stays to defend it.
phases.phase-2:
Thor: The Dark World: Malekith's hunt for the Aether costs Thor his mother, Frigga, killed protecting Jane. He turns down the throne of Asgard afterwards, and tells an Odin who is actually Loki wearing his face.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: a vision in a cave pool shows him Infinity Stones behind everything that has happened, and he leaves Earth to work out what it means.
phases.phase-3:
Doctor Strange: a stop in New York with Loki in tow, which is how Strange ends up involved in Asgardian business at all.
Thor: Ragnarok: it takes the hammer, his father, his eye and his planet, and teaches him that the lightning was never coming from Mjolnir.
Avengers: Infinity War: the opening scene kills half the Asgardians who survived that, along with Loki and Heimdall. Thor forges Stormbreaker, buries it in Thanos's chest, and does not go for the head.
Avengers: Endgame: five years later he is drinking and hiding in New Asgard, and Mjolnir still comes when he calls. He leaves Earth with the Guardians at the end of it.
phases.phase-5: Thor: Love and Thunder: he goes looking for something quieter and finds Gorr the God Butcher instead. Jane Foster is back, dying of cancer, and carrying a reforged Mjolnir that answers to her. Jane dies, Gorr is stopped, and Thor ends the film raising Gorr's daughter.

characters.name: Bruce Banner / Hulk
characters.description: A brilliant scientist whose gamma-radiation accident turns him into a giant green rage monster whenever he loses control.

phases.phase-1:
The Incredible Hulk: a fugitive in Brazil, hiding from General Ross and working on a cure, until Emil Blonsky takes a version of the same serum and forces a fight through Harlem.
The Avengers: Fury's people talk him out of hiding in Kolkata to help find the Tesseract, and he spends most of the film keeping a lid on it until the moment he decides not to.
phases.phase-2:
Iron Man 3: the post-credits only, dozing through Tony's account of the entire film.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: he builds Ultron with Tony out of the Mind Stone, loses control in Johannesburg with Wanda in his head, and decides afterwards that the world is safer without him in it. He flies the Quinjet out and does not say where he is going.
phases.phase-3:
Thor: Ragnarok: the Quinjet came down on Sakaar, and by the time Thor finds him in the arena he has been Hulk without a break for two years.
Avengers: Infinity War: Thanos beats the Hulk in the opening scene, and the Hulk will not come out again for the rest of the film.
Avengers: Endgame: eighteen months in a gamma lab merged the two of them into one person, and it is that version who puts on the gauntlet and brings everyone back, at the cost of his arm.
phases.phase-5:
Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings: the post-credits, back in human form with his arm in a sling, sitting in while Wong examines the Ten Rings.
She-Hulk: Attorney at Law: a car crash puts his blood into his cousin Jennifer and gives her the same condition, and he spends the opening stretch of the series trying to train her out of it. He leaves for Sakaar partway through and comes back with a son, Skaar.

characters.name: Natasha Romanoff / Black Widow
characters.description: A former Russian spy and assassin turned S.H.I.E.L.D. agent, working to wipe the red out of her ledger.

phases.phase-1:
Iron Man 2: introduced undercover as Natalie Rushman inside Stark Industries, sent by Fury to assess Tony for the Avengers Initiative.
The Avengers: she gets what she needs out of Loki by letting him think he is winning, and closes the wormhole over New York.
phases.phase-2:
Captain America: The Winter Soldier: paired with Steve as S.H.I.E.L.D. comes apart, and she puts every classified file the agency holds on the internet to take HYDRA down with it, her own included.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: she is the only one who can bring the Hulk back down, and whatever was starting between her and Banner ends when he flies the Quinjet out.
phases.phase-3:
Captain America: Civil War: she signs the Accords and then lets Steve go at the airport, which leaves her with nowhere to stand on either side.
Black Widow: set immediately after, and it puts her back in front of the fake family she was raised in and the Red Room that made her. She frees Dreykov's Widows.
Avengers: Infinity War: in Scotland with Steve and Sam, then at the Battle of Wakanda.
Avengers: Endgame: the five years in between have her running what is left of the Avengers out of the compound. On Vormir she wins the argument about who goes over the edge.
phases.phase-4: Hawkeye: she does not appear, but the series runs on her death. Yelena spends it hunting the man she has been told is responsible, and finds out on a rooftop what her sister actually chose.

characters.name: Clint Barton / Hawkeye
characters.description: S.H.I.E.L.D.'s master archer, and the Avenger with no powers at all, just aim that does not miss and a family to get home to.

phases.phase-1:
Thor: a few seconds on a crane above the crater site, bow drawn on the man breaking into it.
The Avengers: Loki takes his mind in the opening scene and uses him to steal the Tesseract and wreck the helicarrier, and Natasha has to beat it out of him.
phases.phase-2: Avengers: Age of Ultron: the farm. A wife, three children and a house that appears on no S.H.I.E.L.D. record anywhere, which is the first the rest of the team hears of any of it. He is also the one who talks Wanda out of the corner she has frozen in and into the fight.
phases.phase-3:
Captain America: Civil War: he comes out of retirement for Steve, goes to the Raft for it, and takes a house-arrest deal to get back to his family.
Avengers: Endgame: it opens on the Snap taking his wife and all three children off a field in front of him. He spends the five years after that as Ronin, working through organised crime on several continents. On Vormir he tries to be the one who jumps and loses that argument to Natasha. His family comes back. She does not.
phases.phase-4: Hawkeye: Christmas week in New York, trying to get home to his family while the Ronin suit resurfaces and Kate Bishop attaches herself to him. He deals with Maya Lopez, Yelena Belova and Wilson Fisk, tells Yelena the truth about Natasha on a rooftop, and takes Kate back to the farm for Christmas with the name.

characters.name: Nick Fury
characters.description: Director of S.H.I.E.L.D. and architect of the Avengers Initiative. Always at least three secrets deep.

phases.phase-1:
Iron Man: the post-credits scene, waiting in Tony's living room to talk about the Avengers Initiative.
Iron Man 2: he benches Tony, hands him a case of Howard's old research, and has already put Romanoff inside Stark Industries to watch him.
Thor: the post-credits, showing Erik Selvig a glowing cube and asking him to study it, with Loki standing behind him the whole time.
The Avengers: he assembles the team, loses Coulson, and defies the Council's order to put a nuclear missile into New York.
phases.phase-2:
Captain America: The Winter Soldier: HYDRA ambush him in the street and very nearly kill him, and he fakes his death to work S.H.I.E.L.D.'s collapse from outside it.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: he turns up at Clint's farm with no authority left, and brings a helicarrier to Sokovia when it counts.
phases.phase-3:
Avengers: Infinity War: the credits scene has him dusted mid-sentence, but not before he pages Captain Marvel.
Captain Marvel: set in 1995, with Fury as a desk agent who meets Carol Danvers, finds out what the Skrulls actually are, loses the eye to a cat that is not a cat, and names the Initiative after her call sign.
Avengers: Endgame: back afterwards, and at Tony's funeral.
phases.phase-4: Spider-Man: Far From Home: the Fury shepherding Peter around Europe all film is Talos wearing his face, while the real one works from a Skrull station in orbit.
phases.phase-5:
Secret Invasion: older, tired and off his game. A Skrull faction he made promises to and never kept turns on humanity, and stopping Gravik costs him Maria Hill and Talos.
The Marvels: back upstairs running S.A.B.E.R., handling three heroes who keep swapping places mid-fight.

characters.name: Maria Hill
characters.description: Fury's steely, hyper-competent second-in-command.

phases.phase-1: The Avengers: Fury's second on the helicarrier, questioning every unorthodox call he makes and then carrying it out anyway.
phases.phase-2:
Captain America: The Winter Soldier: helps fake Fury's death and bring down Project Insight.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: working at Stark Industries by now, and still feeding the team intelligence.
phases.phase-3:
Avengers: Infinity War: dusted alongside Fury in the credits scene, mid-sentence.
Avengers: Endgame: back with everyone else, and at Tony's funeral.
phases.phase-4: Spider-Man: Far From Home: the Hill in this one is not her either. She is Soren, Talos's wife, wearing Hill's face while the real one is off-world.
phases.phase-5: Secret Invasion: killed in the opening act, shot by Gravik while he is wearing Fury's face. Her death is what the rest of the series keeps returning to.

characters.name: Phil Coulson
characters.description: The unflappable S.H.I.E.L.D. agent who ties the early films together, and the Avengers' biggest admirer.

phases.phase-1:
Iron Man: the S.H.I.E.L.D. agent who keeps trying to get a meeting with Tony and eventually stops asking politely.
Iron Man 2: minding Tony through the worst of the palladium months, then sent to New Mexico.
Thor: he impounds the crater, confiscates Jane's research, and is unfailingly polite about both.
The Avengers: Loki runs him through, and Fury uses his death, and his set of vintage trading cards, to give a bickering team a reason to work together.
phases.phase-3: Captain Marvel: set in 1995, with Coulson as a rookie riding along with Fury years before any of the rest of it.

characters.name: Loki
characters.description: Thor's adopted brother and the God of Mischief. Sometimes a villain, sometimes an ally, always working an angle.

phases.phase-1:
Thor: he finds out he is a Frost Giant foundling Odin took from Jotunheim, and it curdles into a grab for the throne that ends with him letting go of the spear into the void.
The Avengers: he comes back with the scepter as the face of the Chitauri invasion, and the Hulk puts him through a floor.
phases.phase-2: Thor: The Dark World: let out of his cell to help avenge Frigga, the one person he never stopped caring about. He fakes his death on Svartalfheim and takes the throne of Asgard wearing Odin's face.
phases.phase-3:
Thor: Ragnarok: Hela knocks him and Thor out of the Bifrost and he lands on Sakaar, where he talks his way into the Grandmaster's good books. He goes back for Asgard and pockets the Tesseract while it burns.
Avengers: Infinity War: that Tesseract is why Thanos finds them, and the film opens with Thanos killing him for it. No resurrections this time.
Avengers: Endgame: the 2012 version of him grabs the Tesseract during the time heist and vanishes with it.
phases.phase-4:
Loki: Season 1: the TVA arrest that 2012 variant for stepping off the Sacred Timeline. Mobius, Sylvie, and a citadel at the end of time where the man who built the whole apparatus offers him the job.
Loki: Season 2: he learns to steer his own time-slipping, spends centuries failing to save everyone, and then takes the Loom's place himself, holding every branch alone at the end of time. The God of Stories.

characters.name: Sam Wilson / Falcon
characters.description: A pararescue veteran with a winged flight suit, and Steve Rogers' most loyal partner.

phases.phase-2:
Captain America: The Winter Soldier: a VA counsellor Steve keeps lapping on a morning run, who puts the EXO-7 Falcon wings back on the moment Steve asks.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: on the new Avengers roster by the end of it.
phases.phase-3:
Ant-Man: he fights Scott Lang in a compound hangar, loses, and asks him not to tell Steve.
Captain America: Civil War: sides with Steve, goes to the Raft for it, and spends the next two years a fugitive.
Avengers: Infinity War: dusted at the Battle of Wakanda.
Avengers: Endgame: he is the voice in Steve's earpiece saying on your left, and afterwards an old Steve Rogers hands him the shield.
phases.phase-4: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: he gives the shield to a museum, watches the government hand it to John Walker, and learns what the super soldier programme did to Isaiah Bradley. He takes the name anyway, on his own terms, in a suit Wakanda built for him.
phases.phase-6: Captain America: Brave New World: the title without the serum. A conspiracy around President Ross, an assassination attempt, the scramble for adamantium, and a Red Hulk over Washington. He also brings Joaquin Torres in as the new Falcon.

characters.name: Bucky Barnes
characters.description: Steve Rogers' childhood best friend and WWII brother-in-arms, whose story doesn't end where the history books say it does.

phases.phase-1: Captain America: The First Avenger: Steve's protector since they were boys in Brooklyn, a sergeant in the 107th, rescued by Steve from Zola's lab and then lost off a train in the Alps. The history books stop there.
phases.phase-2: Captain America: The Winter Soldier: HYDRA had him the whole time. Seventy years as their assassin, kept frozen between jobs, memory wiped each time, no record of him anywhere. Sent to kill Steve, something surfaces late enough that he pulls him out of the Potomac and disappears.
phases.phase-3:
Ant-Man: the mid-credits, his metal arm clamped in a vice in a warehouse while Steve and Sam work out who they can safely call.
Captain America: Civil War: the film is fought over him. Zemo frames him for the Vienna bombing, uses the trigger words to turn him loose, and then shows Tony the tape of his handlers making him kill the Starks.
Black Panther: the post-credits, out of cryo in a Wakandan village, being called White Wolf by the children.
Avengers: Infinity War: fights at Wakanda and is one of the first to go when the Snap lands.
Avengers: Endgame: back for the final battle, and entirely unsurprised when Steve chooses to stay in the past.
phases.phase-4: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: court-ordered therapy, a list of amends he is working through, and a great deal of arguing with Sam. He makes peace with some of the people the Winter Soldier hurt, and pushes Sam towards the shield.
phases.phase-6: Thunderbolts*: a congressman, of all things, until Valentina's schemes pull him back into the field with a team of misfits who end the film rebranded as the New Avengers.

characters.name: James "Rhodey" Rhodes / War Machine
characters.description: Air Force officer, Tony Stark's best friend, and pilot of his own heavily armed suit of armor.

phases.phase-1:
Iron Man: Tony's military liaison and the closest thing he has to a conscience.
Iron Man 2: he takes the Mark II out of the house during Tony's birthday meltdown, and the Air Force turns it into War Machine.
phases.phase-2:
Iron Man 3: repainted and rebranded as the Iron Patriot, which nobody is enthusiastic about. He is the one who pulls the President off the Extremis rig.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: on the roster by now, and at the party trying to tell a war story nobody is listening to.
phases.phase-3:
Captain America: Civil War: he signs the Accords, and a friendly-fire blast at the airport drops him out of the sky and costs him the use of his legs.
Avengers: Infinity War: back in the air on Stark leg braces, at the Battle of Wakanda.
Avengers: Endgame: on the time heist, sent to Morag with Nebula.
phases.phase-5: Secret Invasion: the Rhodey advising President Ritson is a Skrull, and has been for long enough to matter. The real one is unconscious in a pod until the finale.

characters.name: Wanda Maximoff / Scarlet Witch
characters.description: A Sokovian orphan who gained telekinetic and mind-warping powers through HYDRA experiments with the Mind Stone.

phases.phase-2:
Captain America: The Winter Soldier: the post-credits, in a cell in Strucker's HYDRA base with her brother, moving objects without touching them.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: she and Pietro are Sokovian orphans who volunteered for HYDRA's scepter experiments to get at Stark. She takes the Avengers apart with nightmare visions, switches sides once she reads Ultron's actual plan, and loses Pietro in the same battle.
phases.phase-3:
Captain America: Civil War: the accident in Lagos, where her containment of a blast goes wrong, is what the Accords are written in response to. She ends the film in the Raft and then on the run.
Avengers: Infinity War: she destroys the Mind Stone in Vision's head at his request, and Thanos rewinds time and takes it out of him anyway, in front of her.
Avengers: Endgame: back through the portals, and she gets Thanos on his own for about thirty seconds.
phases.phase-4:
WandaVision: her grief rewrites the town of Westview into a run of sitcom decades, with a rebuilt Vision and two sons she conjures. Agatha forces the truth out of her, and she walks out of it as the Scarlet Witch with the Darkhold.
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness: the Darkhold winning. She goes after America Chavez's power to reach a universe where her sons are real, kills the Illuminati of Earth-838 on the way, and stops only when her own boys look at her in terror. She brings Mount Wundagore down on herself.

characters.name: Pietro Maximoff / Quicksilver
characters.description: Wanda's twin brother, fast enough that the rest of the world seems frozen.

phases.phase-2:
Captain America: The Winter Soldier: the post-credits, in the cell next to his sister in Strucker's base, moving too fast to follow.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: the Sokovian twin who volunteered for the scepter experiments alongside Wanda, switches sides with her, and dies taking a burst of gunfire meant for Clint and a child.
phases.phase-4: WandaVision: the Pietro who turns up is not him. It is a Westview local called Ralph Bohner, puppeteered by Agatha to pick at Wanda's grief.

characters.name: Vision
characters.description: A synthetic being born from an artificial intelligence and the Mind Stone. Thoughtful, immensely powerful, and quietly human.

phases.phase-2: Avengers: Age of Ultron: built as Ultron's intended body, then hijacked and woken by the Avengers with JARVIS's mind and the Mind Stone in his forehead. He settles the argument about whether to trust him by handing Thor Mjolnir, and he is the one who destroys Ultron's last body.
phases.phase-3:
Captain America: Civil War: on Tony's side, and his one misfired blast is what puts Rhodey in the ground. His attachment to Wanda deepens while the two of them are on opposite sides of the fight.
Avengers: Infinity War: the stone in his head makes him the target. Wanda destroys it, and him, at his own request, and Thanos rewinds time and pulls it out of his skull anyway.
phases.phase-4: WandaVision: two of him. The Westview Vision is built out of Wanda's grief and memory and goes when the Hex goes. White Vision is S.W.O.R.D. reactivating the real body as a weapon, and he leaves at the end carrying the original's memories and no clear idea of what he is.

characters.name: Billy Maximoff / Wiccan
characters.description: One of Wanda's twin sons, born inside Westview, with his mother's talent for magic.

phases.phase-4:
WandaVision: conjured rather than conceived. Wanda's pregnancy runs its course in a single episode inside the Hex, and the twins are born the same day. They age themselves to five and then to ten because the sitcom needs them to, and Billy's powers arrive with the growth spurt. He hears thoughts, and by the finale he is throwing magic in a way that plainly comes from his mother. When Wanda takes the Hex down, both boys go with it, and she tells them she will find them again.
Agatha All Along: the Teen who springs Agatha from the Agnes persona and will not give his name, because a sigil stops him saying it out loud. He is Billy. When the Hex fell his consciousness landed in William Kaplan, a boy who died in a car crash at that exact moment, and he has been living that boy's life with that boy's parents ever since. He takes the name Wiccan, and the series ends with him setting out to find Tommy, with Agatha's ghost attached to him.

characters.name: Tommy Maximoff / Speed
characters.description: One of Wanda's twin sons, born inside Westview, who takes after his uncle rather than his mother.

phases.phase-4:
WandaVision: born alongside Billy inside the Hex and aged up the same way. His power is speed, which is not a coincidence, since Pietro is a large part of why Wanda's grief built any of this. He goes when the Hex goes.
Agatha All Along: not seen, but the reason Billy is on the Road at all. Billy works out that if his own consciousness landed somewhere when the Hex fell, Tommy's could have too, and the series ends with him going to look.

characters.name: Sharon Davis / Mrs. Hart
characters.description: A Westview resident, and one of the few people caught up in Wanda's sitcom who turns up again afterwards.

phases.phase-4:
WandaVision: cast as the boss's wife in the first episode, at the dinner party that goes wrong. Wanda tells her to stop laughing and she cannot stop, which is the earliest sign that nobody in the town is choosing anything they do. She is one of the residents Wanda releases at the end.
Agatha All Along: still in Westview and still going by Mrs. Hart, which is not her name. She attaches herself to Agatha's coven as their green witch, having no power at all, and walks the Witches' Road on enthusiasm. It does not go well for her.

characters.name: Peter Parker / Spider-Man
characters.description: A Queens high-schooler juggling homework and web-slinging, taken under Tony Stark's wing.

phases.phase-3:
Captain America: Civil War: Stark recruits him out of Queens for the airport fight, and he is still hiding all of it from Aunt May.
Spider-Man: Homecoming: the Vulture, who turns out to be his homecoming date's father. He turns down a place on the Avengers to stay a neighbourhood hero.
Avengers: Infinity War: dragged to Titan anyway, where he dusts in Tony's arms.
Avengers: Endgame: back through the portals, and at the funeral afterwards.
phases.phase-4:
Spider-Man: Far From Home: Tony's legacy, EDITH, and Quentin Beck's con, which ends with his identity broadcast to the world and a murder pinned on him.
Spider-Man: No Way Home: a botched memory spell cracks the multiverse and pulls in villains, and two other Peter Parkers, from universes where they already knew who he was. He loses May to the Green Goblin, chooses to cure the villains rather than send them back to die, and ends the film having Strange erase Peter Parker from every mind on Earth. Last seen alone in a bedsit with a homemade suit and a GED study guide.

characters.name: Stephen Strange / Doctor Strange
characters.description: An arrogant, world-class surgeon who loses the use of his hands and finds the mystic arts instead.

phases.phase-3:
Doctor Strange: a car crash ends his surgical career, and the search for a fix lands him at Kamar-Taj. He beats Dormammu by trapping him in a time loop rather than a fight, and takes the New York Sanctum.
Thor: Ragnarok: a stop in the middle, relocating Thor and Loki out of his house and pointing them at Norway.
Avengers: Infinity War: he looks at fourteen million possible futures, finds the one where they win, and hands Thanos the Time Stone to keep Tony alive for it.
Avengers: Endgame: the portals, and the raised finger telling Tony this is the one.
phases.phase-4:
Spider-Man: No Way Home: he casts the memory spell that cracks the multiverse open, then a harder one that erases Peter from everybody who ever knew him.
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness: universe-hopping to keep America Chavez away from Wanda, dreamwalking into the corpse of a dead variant to get home, and coming out of it with a third eye.

characters.name: T'Challa / Black Panther
characters.description: King and protector of Wakanda, the hidden, hyper-advanced African nation.

phases.phase-3:
Captain America: Civil War: introduced in the middle of a tragedy. His father is killed in the Vienna bombing, and his hunt for Bucky ends with him deciding not to let Zemo have him too.
Black Panther: the coronation, Killmonger's challenge, and the argument about what Wakanda owes everyone outside it. It ends with Wakanda telling the world what it actually is.
Avengers: Infinity War: he hosts the last stand at Wakanda and dusts on the field.
Avengers: Endgame: back through the portals for the final battle.
phases.phase-5: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: he does not appear. The film opens with his death from an illness nobody could treat in time, and the story is Wakanda, and Shuri in particular, learning to live without him. The ending reveals he had a son, Toussaint, whose Wakandan name is T'Challa.

characters.name: Carol Danvers / Captain Marvel
characters.description: A U.S. Air Force pilot turned cosmic powerhouse, caught in the middle of an alien war.

phases.phase-3:
Captain Marvel: set in 1995. A Kree soldier called Vers crash-lands into her own erased past, works out she is a human test pilot named Carol Danvers, and that the people who trained her are the ones who took her memory. She unlocks the full extent of what the core did to her, sends the Skrull refugees off to find a home, and leaves Fury a modified pager.
Avengers: Endgame: the pager gets answered. She hauls Tony and Nebula home from space, takes Thanos's flagship apart on her own, and gets a hand on the gauntlet.
phases.phase-5:
Ms. Marvel: the post-credits, standing in Kamala's bedroom having swapped places with her and visibly confused about it.
The Marvels: her light powers are entangled with Kamala's and Monica's, so the three of them swap places mid-fight. Dar-Benn is fallout from Carol's own war on the Kree, who call her the Annihilator. She ends it by reigniting Hala's sun.

characters.name: Maria Rambeau
characters.description: A former United States Air Force pilot and Carol Danvers' best friend, who becomes a skilled fighter pilot and a loving mother of Monica Rambeau.

phases.phase-3: Captain Marvel: an Air Force test pilot who flew with Carol under the call sign Photon, and who was told her best friend died in a crash. Six years on she is the one who fills in the past Carol cannot remember, and she flies the mission to Mar-Vell's hidden lab alongside her. She takes Minn-Erva out of the sky during the chase over the desert.
phases.phase-4:
WandaVision: her death is filled in here rather than shown. She ran S.W.O.R.D. after Carol left, was diagnosed with cancer in 2018, lost Monica in the Snap while she was in hospital, and died in 2020, three years before her daughter came back.
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness: a variant of her on Earth-838 is that world's Captain Marvel, and one of the Illuminati Wanda kills.
phases.phase-5: The Marvels: another version of her again, this one operating as Binary alongside the X-Men, in the universe Monica ends up stranded in.

characters.name: Yon-Rogg
characters.description: Yon-Rogg is a high-ranking military leader for the Kree Empire who runs an elite team called Starforce. He completely believes in the Kree way of life and is totally loyal to their leader, the Supreme Intelligence.

phases.phase-3: Captain Marvel: a Kree commander sent to Earth with Minn-Erva to find Mar-Vell and take the energy core she had built. The core was destroyed in the fight and an American test pilot absorbed what came out of it, so Yon-Rogg took her back to Hala, named her Vers, and spent six years training her and telling her the power was his to give and take away. When she finds out Earth is her home and that the Kree lied to her about all of it, he gets Ronan's permission to bring her in. She refuses to fight him on his terms, puts him flat on his back, and sends him home with a message for the Supreme Intelligence.

characters.name: Goose the Flerken
characters.description: A cat-like alien with tentacles and a pocket dimension in its stomach.

phases.phase-3: Captain Marvel: a Flerken, which looks exactly like a cat right up until it does not. She belonged to Mar-Vell, joins Carol and Fury on the trip to the hidden lab, swallows the Tesseract to keep it away from the Kree, and takes Fury's left eye with one swipe.
phases.phase-5: The Marvels: Fury finds her nesting in a wall panel on the S.A.B.E.R. station, surrounded by eggs. When the station has to be evacuated in a hurry, the kittens swallow the entire crew and bring them back out on Earth.

characters.name: Scott Lang / Ant-Man
characters.description: An ex-con and well-meaning dad who inherits a suit that can shrink him to insect size.

phases.phase-3:
Ant-Man: an ex-burglar out of prison and short of options, recruited by Hank Pym to steal back his own suit and stop Darren Cross selling the Yellowjacket. He goes subatomic to get through Cross's armour and comes back out again, which nobody thought was possible. All of it is so that Cassie has something to be proud of.
Captain America: Civil War: he turns up for the airport fight, goes Giant-Man in front of everyone, and gets house arrest for it.
Ant-Man and the Wasp: the tail end of that house arrest, and the mission to pull Janet out of the Quantum Realm. The credits scene strands him down there mid-Snap while all three Pyms turn to dust.
Avengers: Endgame: five years later a rat knocks the switch and lets him out. He walks into the compound with the idea that becomes the time heist.
phases.phase-4: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania: a memoir tour interrupted when Cassie's beacon pulls the whole family into the Quantum Realm, where the exile Janet never talked about needs a way out. He beats a multiversal warlord with ants and refusal, and tries not to think about how many more of him are out there.

characters.name: Hope van Dyne / Wasp
characters.description: Hank Pym's fiercely capable daughter, who fights with wings, blasters, and shrinking tech of her own.

phases.phase-3:
Ant-Man: she trains Scott to do a job she could do better herself, because Hank will not risk losing her the way he lost Janet. The mid-credits finally shows her the wings.
Ant-Man and the Wasp: she runs the operation to get her mother out of the Quantum Realm and out-fights everyone else in the film doing it. She dusts in the credits scene mid-operation, along with both her parents.
Avengers: Endgame: back for the final battle.
phases.phase-4: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania: running the Pym van Dyne Foundation when Cassie's beacon pulls the family under. She fights Kang alongside Scott and gets them home.

characters.name: Shang-Chi
characters.description: A San Francisco valet with a hidden past as the meticulously trained son of a legendary warlord.

phases.phase-5: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings: a San Francisco valet called Shaun, who is actually the son of Wenwu, the man who has run the Ten Rings organisation for a thousand years, and who trained him from the age of seven to be an assassin. Going home means facing his sister Xialing and his father's conviction that his dead wife is being held somewhere behind the gates of Ta Lo. Wenwu is killed by the thing he was trying to let out, and Shang-Chi takes the rings. The post-credits establishes that they are far older than anyone thought, and that they are signalling something.

characters.name: Kamala Khan / Ms. Marvel
characters.description: A Jersey City teen and Avengers superfan whose grandmother's bangle unlocks cosmic light powers.

phases.phase-5:
Ms. Marvel: a bangle handed down from her great-grandmother wakes hard-light powers tied to the Noor dimension, and the family history behind it runs back to the Partition of India, where a time slip reveals Kamala herself was the trail of stars that saved her own grandmother. The finale mentions, almost in passing, that there is something different in her genes.
The Marvels: the bangle entangles her light powers with Carol's and Monica's, so the three of them swap places mid-fight. She holds her own, loses the matching bangle to Dar-Benn, and in the post-credits turns up in Kate Bishop's flat recruiting for a team.

characters.name: Jennifer Walters / She-Hulk
characters.description: Bruce Banner's cousin, a lawyer who gets Hulk powers and would really rather just do her job.

phases.phase-5: She-Hulk: Attorney at Law: a car crash puts Bruce's blood into hers, and she skips the years of rage management he needed, which she is tired of being congratulated for. She runs a superhuman law division, takes Emil Blonsky on as a client, gets doxxed and blood-harvested by the Intelligencia, and when the finale stops making sense she climbs out of the show to argue with the writing about it.

characters.name: Marc Spector / Moon Knight
characters.description: A mercenary sharing his body with a mild-mannered gift-shop clerk, serving an Egyptian moon god as its avatar.

phases.phase-5: Moon Knight: a London gift-shop clerk called Steven Grant works out he is sharing a body with Marc Spector, a mercenary who serves the moon god Khonshu. Arthur Harrow is hunting both of them so he can free the judgment goddess Ammit. It runs through tomb raiding in Egypt, a psychiatric ward that may be an afterlife, the scales of the Duat, and the childhood that split Marc in the first place. The post-credits reveals a third alter, Jake Lockley, who has been doing Khonshu's killing all along.

characters.name: Kate Bishop
characters.description: A 22-year-old archery prodigy who idolizes Hawkeye and stumbles headfirst into his old mess.

phases.phase-4: Hawkeye: she puts the Ronin suit on at a black-market auction and inherits every enemy it ever made, from the Tracksuit Mafia to Maya Lopez to Wilson Fisk, who turns out to be working with her own mother. A week of that later she is Clint's actual partner, and she has the name.
phases.phase-5: The Marvels: the post-credits, with Kamala Khan standing in her flat at night, extremely pleased with herself, pitching a team.

characters.name: Yelena Belova
characters.description: Natasha's younger 'sister' from her spy days. Funnier, arguably deadlier, and finished being used.

phases.phase-3: Black Widow: the other daughter from the fake family in Ohio, raised into the Red Room's chemically controlled generation of Widows. The antidote frees her, and she frees the rest of them. The credits scene jumps forward to Yelena at Natasha's grave, being pointed at Clint Barton by Valentina.
phases.phase-4: Hawkeye: she spends Christmas week stalking Clint to avenge Natasha, and stops when he whistles the signal the two sisters used and she understands he loved her too.
phases.phase-6: Thunderbolts*: hollowed out and doing Valentina's disposal work on her own, until she is dropped into a containment room with the rest of the deniable assets. She walks into Bob's Void to pull him out of it, dragging her own worst memory behind her, and comes out the closest thing the New Avengers have to a centre.

characters.name: Monica Rambeau
characters.description: Daughter of Carol Danvers' best friend, who grows up to become a S.W.O.R.D. agent with a bigger role ahead of her.

phases.phase-3: Captain Marvel: eleven years old, Maria's daughter, and called Lieutenant Trouble. She helps pick the colours for Carol's suit and watches her leave.
phases.phase-4: WandaVision: first seen inside the sitcom as Geraldine, the neighbour who never quite fits. She is Captain Monica Rambeau of S.W.O.R.D., blipped for five years and back to find her mother died of cancer while she was gone. When she pushes Wanda about Pietro, Wanda throws her out through the barrier. Going back through it a second time rewrites her at a cellular level, which is where the powers come from.
phases.phase-5: The Marvels: entangled with Carol and Kamala, and working through the years she spent waiting for Carol to come back. She closes Dar-Benn's rift from the wrong side of it and wakes in another universe entirely, in a hospital bed, with her mother's face looking down at her and a woman taking notes who is plainly not from around here.

characters.name: America Chavez
characters.description: A teenager who can punch holes between universes, and who has no idea how to control it.

phases.phase-4: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness: as far as anyone can tell the only America Chavez in the multiverse, orphaned by her own untrained power and hunted across realities by the Scarlet Witch, who wants to take the ability out of her. She ends the film able to use it on purpose, training at Kamar-Taj.

characters.name: Jane Foster
characters.description: The astrophysicist who discovers Thor, and whose story with the hammer is not over.

phases.phase-1: Thor: the scientist who runs into Thor in the New Mexico desert, twice, with a van. Her research into wormholes turns out to be the Bifrost.
phases.phase-2: Thor: The Dark World: she becomes the Aether's unwilling host, carrying an Infinity Stone in her bloodstream, and it takes her to Asgard, where Frigga dies protecting her.
phases.phase-3: Avengers: Endgame: the time heist drops Thor and Rocket into Asgard in 2013 to pull the Aether back out of her, so she appears without ever knowing she was in the film. It is also the last time Thor sees his mother.
phases.phase-5: Thor: Love and Thunder: years after the breakup, stage-four cancer leads her to the shards of Mjolnir, and the hammer reforges around her. As the Mighty Thor she fights Gorr knowing that every transformation burns through what the chemotherapy bought her. She dies in Thor's arms and the film puts her in Valhalla.

characters.name: Valkyrie
characters.description: A hard-drinking former member of Asgard's legendary all-female warrior order.

phases.phase-3:
Thor: Ragnarok: found on Sakaar as Scrapper 142, drinking to forget being the only survivor of the Valkyrior's charge against Hela. She sobers up enough to join the Revengers and fly the refugees off a dying Asgard.
Avengers: Endgame: back for the final battle, and Thor hands her New Asgard in the epilogue.
phases.phase-5: Thor: Love and Thunder: King Valkyrie, bored senseless by ribbon-cuttings and delighted to be back in the field against Gorr, where she is wounded badly enough to sit the ending out.

characters.name: Matt Murdock / Daredevil
characters.description: A blind Hell's Kitchen lawyer with radar-sharp senses and a nighttime hobby.

phases.phase-4:
Spider-Man: No Way Home: Peter's lawyer, who gets the charges dropped in about a minute and catches a brick thrown through the window without looking at it.
Echo: the flashbacks put him in Maya Lopez's path back in New York, in a warehouse fight that is a reminder of what he does after dark.
phases.phase-5: She-Hulk: Attorney at Law: the yellow-and-red armour, a hallway fight, and a walk of shame out of Jen's flat the following morning.

characters.name: Maya Lopez / Echo
characters.description: A deaf Choctaw enforcer in New York's underworld who can perfectly mirror any fighting style she sees.

phases.phase-4:
Hawkeye: a lieutenant in the Tracksuit Mafia hunting Ronin, the vigilante who killed her father. The truth is worse than that, because her uncle Wilson Fisk arranged the killing. The season ends with her shooting him at point-blank range.
Echo: on the run from Fisk's people, she goes home to Tamaha and the Choctaw family she left. Abilities inherited down a line of ancestors surface in her, and instead of taking the empire Fisk offers she turns that power on him and makes him look at his own childhood. She stays. He leaves.

characters.name: Riri Williams / Ironheart
characters.description: An MIT genius building her own suit of armor.

phases.phase-5:
Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: a student whose classroom-project vibranium detector paints a target on her, and both Wakanda and Talokan come for her. She builds her Mark II in Shuri's lab and flies it in the final battle, then goes home with the design in her head rather than her hands.
Ironheart: back in Chicago and building the suit properly this time, on no budget and with the wrong sort of funding.

characters.name: Cassie Lang
characters.description: Scott's daughter, who grows up idolizing her dad and wanting in on the hero business.

phases.phase-3:
Ant-Man: six years old, and the reason Scott is doing any of it. Delighted by the giant ant he leaves in her bedroom.
Ant-Man and the Wasp: ten, and helping from the back of the van.
Avengers: Endgame: the Blip skipped her from ten to fifteen, and Scott coming home to a daughter who grew up without him is the quietest thing in the film.
phases.phase-4: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania: a teenage activist with an arrest record and a suit of her own. Her Quantum Realm beacon is what drags the whole family down there, and she fights, frees prisoners, and earns the suit properly.

characters.name: Peter Quill / Star-Lord
characters.description: A human abducted from Earth as a kid, now a wisecracking outlaw with a walkman full of '70s hits.

phases.phase-2:
Guardians of the Galaxy: he steals the wrong orb and ends up with an Infinity Stone, a bounty on his head, and four people who cannot stand each other. He holds the Power Stone long enough for the others to grab on, and survives it because he is half something else.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2: the answer to what that half is. His father is Ego, a living planet, who put the tumour in his mother's head. He kills him with the family he picked instead, and buries Yondu.
phases.phase-3:
Avengers: Infinity War: he finds Gamora again, and then finds out on Titan that Thanos has already killed her. He hits Thanos, and the plan that was working stops working.
Avengers: Endgame: back for the battle, and afterwards going through star charts looking for a Gamora who has never met him.
phases.phase-5:
Thor: Love and Thunder: the Guardians drop Thor off at the start and go their own way.
The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special: the crew kidnaps Kevin Bacon to cheer him up at Christmas, and it works better than it has any right to.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3: he drinks through the Gamora of it, then holds together long enough to take the High Evolutionary's empire apart for Rocket. He hands the team over and goes home to Missouri.

characters.name: Gamora
characters.description: The deadliest woman in the galaxy, raised as a weapon by Thanos and looking for a way out.

phases.phase-2:
Guardians of the Galaxy: sent by Ronan for the orb and defects instead, betraying him and Thanos in the same move.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2: the start of something workable with Nebula, after a fight that wrecks a good deal of Ego's planet.
phases.phase-3:
Avengers: Infinity War: Thanos takes her, tortures Nebula in front of her to get the location of the Soul Stone, and then throws her off the cliff on Vormir, because the stone costs you whatever you love.
Avengers: Endgame: a 2014 version of her comes forward with Thanos, defects again on principle, and walks away after the battle.
phases.phase-5: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3: that variant is running with the Ravagers when the crew needs her, and she spends the film being grieved at by people she has never met. She is not their Gamora and the film does not pretend otherwise. She leaves having picked her own crew.

characters.name: Drax the Destroyer
characters.description: A relentlessly literal-minded warrior on a quest to avenge his murdered family.

phases.phase-2:
Guardians of the Galaxy: in the Kyln for going after Ronan, who killed his wife and daughter. He calls Ronan in early and nearly gets everyone killed, and gets his hands on him in the end.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2: mostly Mantis, the only person in the galaxy more literal than he is.
phases.phase-3:
Avengers: Infinity War: on Titan, holding perfectly still, and dusting with the rest of them.
Avengers: Endgame: back through the portals.
phases.phase-5:
Thor: Love and Thunder: on the ship at the start, then gone.
The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special: co-architect of the Kevin Bacon abduction.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3: the film decides he is not a destroyer but a father, and he is the only one who can talk to the children the High Evolutionary engineered. He stays on Knowhere to help raise them.

characters.name: Rocket
characters.description: A genetically engineered raccoon: weapons expert, ace pilot, and professional cynic.

phases.phase-2:
Guardians of the Galaxy: a bounty hunter and jailbreak specialist who does not talk about where the cybernetics came from.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2: he and Yondu recognise the same thing in each other, and neither of them enjoys it.
phases.phase-3:
Avengers: Infinity War: the only original Guardian left standing after the Snap.
Avengers: Endgame: five years as an actual Avenger, and the one who builds the tech the heist runs on.
phases.phase-5:
Thor: Love and Thunder: on the ship at the start, glad to see the back of Thor.
The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special: the running joke about Bucky Barnes’ old arm pays off here. He bought it, and it is his now.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3: his film. Flashbacks to the High Evolutionary's cages and the three friends who never got out of them, while the crew races to keep him alive in the present. He meets his maker, opens the cages, and ends it captain of the Guardians.

characters.name: Groot
characters.description: A walking tree with a three-word vocabulary and a heart bigger than his trunk.

phases.phase-2:
Guardians of the Galaxy: muscle and houseplant, who wraps himself around the others when the ship goes down and does not survive it. The twig that gets kept becomes Baby Groot.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2: Baby Groot, mostly fetching the wrong thing.
phases.phase-3:
Avengers: Infinity War: teenage, monosyllabic, and the one who gives Thor an arm for Stormbreaker's handle. Dusts at Wakanda.
Avengers: Endgame: back for the battle.
phases.phase-5:
Thor: Love and Thunder: on the ship at the start.
The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special: large, festive, and decorated.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3: fully grown, and the last thing he says is the first thing anyone else can understand.

characters.name: Nebula
characters.description: Thanos' other daughter, part machine, driven by rivalry with Gamora and rage at her father.

phases.phase-2:
Guardians of the Galaxy: Ronan's enforcer, and the daughter Thanos replaced a piece of every time Gamora beat her.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2: the sisters finally have the argument, and she leaves to go and kill Thanos herself.
phases.phase-3:
Avengers: Infinity War: captured and taken apart while she is still conscious, to make Gamora talk.
Avengers: Endgame: the heist runs through her twice. Her networked memory is how the 2014 Thanos finds out about it, and she is the one who shoots her own past self.
phases.phase-5:
Thor: Love and Thunder: on the ship at the start.
The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special: on Knowhere, unimpressed with all of it.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3: rebuilt, with a new arm and firm opinions about its settings, and effectively the adult in the room. She stays behind to run Knowhere.

characters.name: Mantis
characters.description: An empath who can feel and alter emotions with a touch. Naive, gentle, and funnier than she intends to be.

phases.phase-2: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2: kept by Ego to put him to sleep and treated like a pet until somebody treats her otherwise. Her friendship with Drax is the oddest thing in the film.
phases.phase-3:
Avengers: Infinity War: she is the one holding Thanos under on Titan when the plan falls apart. Dusts with the others.
Avengers: Endgame: back for the battle.
phases.phase-5:
Thor: Love and Thunder: on the ship at the start.
The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special: she is Quill's half-sister, another of Ego's children, and she says so in the middle of a musical number.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3: done being underestimated. She leaves at the end to find out who she is when she is not managing everyone else's feelings.

characters.name: Yondu Udonta
characters.description: The blue-skinned Ravager captain who "raised" Peter Quill, armed with a whistle-controlled arrow.

phases.phase-2:
Guardians of the Galaxy: the Ravager hired to deliver Quill to his father, who kept him instead and spent twenty years insisting it was because the boy was small enough to fit through vents.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2: he kept him because he knew what Ego did to the others. He gives Quill the only spacesuit and dies for it, and the Ravagers give him the funeral they threw him out of.

characters.name: Kraglin
characters.description: Yondu's scrappy, endlessly loyal first mate.

phases.phase-2:
Guardians of the Galaxy: Yondu's first mate, in the background of most of it.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2: one complaint of his is what turns into the mutiny that costs Yondu his crew. He inherits the fin afterwards, and an arrow he cannot whistle straight.
phases.phase-5:
The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special: still on Knowhere, still practising.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3: he gets the arrow right in the middle of a fight, and takes a place on the new roster.

characters.name: Adam Warlock
characters.description: A golden artificial being engineered by the Sovereign to be perfect, and decanted a little early.

phases.phase-2: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2: the credits scene only. Ayesha, humiliated, shows off a birthing pod with her next creation inside it, and gives him a name.
phases.phase-5: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3: hatched early and sent after Rocket, enormously powerful and emotionally about six years old. He fails at nearly everything he is sent to do, acquires a pet, and ends the film on the team more or less by accident.

characters.name: Pepper Potts
characters.description: Tony Stark's indispensable right hand, and the one person who can actually manage him.

phases.phase-1:
Iron Man: Tony's assistant, and the one who pulls the old reactor out of his chest and puts the new one in. She overloads the big reactor in the workshop to finish Obadiah Stane.
Iron Man 2: he makes her CEO of Stark Industries, largely so that he does not have to be.
The Avengers: briefly, at the tower, just before the sky opens over it.
phases.phase-2: Iron Man 3: kidnapped by Killian and injected with Extremis, which she then uses to put him through his own explosion. The Extremis is burned back out of her afterwards.
phases.phase-3:
Spider-Man: Homecoming: at the compound at the end, for a press conference that Tony turns into a proposal.
Avengers: Infinity War: a jog in Central Park, an argument about the dream he keeps having, and then the ring.
Avengers: Endgame: married, with a daughter called Morgan, in the five years everyone else lost. She flies the Rescue armour in the final battle, and she is the one who tells Tony he can rest.

characters.name: Happy Hogan
characters.description: Stark's driver, head of security, and reluctant den mother to younger heroes.

phases.phase-1:
Iron Man: Tony's driver, and the closest thing he has to staff who will argue back.
Iron Man 2: he lands exactly one punch during Natasha's corridor fight, and is very pleased with it.
phases.phase-2: Iron Man 3: promoted to head of security and blown into a coma investigating Extremis, which is why Tony gives the Mandarin his home address on television.
phases.phase-3:
Captain America: Civil War: still running Tony's security, in the background of the Accords fallout.
Spider-Man: Homecoming: Peter's exasperated handler, and the man who never listens to his voicemails.
Avengers: Endgame: at the funeral, and looking after Morgan afterwards.
phases.phase-4:
Spider-Man: Far From Home: grief counsellor on a jet, and the start of a thing with May.
Spider-Man: No Way Home: he harbours fugitive Spider-Men, loses the condo, and at May's grave cannot work out why the boy at the funeral matters to him.

characters.name: Peggy Carter
characters.description: A founding agent of S.H.I.E.L.D. and the great love of Steve Rogers' life.

phases.phase-1: Captain America: The First Avenger: an SSR officer who believes in Steve before the serum does anything for him, and the voice on the radio when he puts the plane into the ice. The dance never happens.
phases.phase-2:
Captain America: The Winter Soldier: Steve visits her in care. She founded S.H.I.E.L.D., she is in her nineties, and she loses him mid-conversation and grieves him again from the beginning.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: she is in the vision Wanda puts in Steve's head, at the dance he never got to.
phases.phase-3:
Ant-Man: the 1989 flashback, on the other side of the table when Hank Pym resigns.
Captain America: Civil War: it opens with her funeral, and the eulogy Sharon gives is what points Steve where he goes next.
Avengers: Endgame: the dance, finally. The last shot of the Infinity Saga is the two of them in her living room.

characters.name: Sharon Carter
characters.description: Peggy's niece, and a highly trained agent who keeps ending up on the wrong side of official orders.

phases.phase-2: Captain America: The Winter Soldier: introduced as Kate, the nurse across the hall, and actually a S.H.I.E.L.D. agent assigned to watch Steve. She is one of the few who refuses HYDRA at gunpoint.
phases.phase-3: Captain America: Civil War: she gives the eulogy at Peggy's funeral, steals Team Cap's gear back for them, and loses her career over it.
phases.phase-4: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: the years she spent abandoned in Madripoor turned her into the Power Broker, which the season only admits at the end. The tag is worse: pardoned, reinstated, and already selling what she can reach.

characters.name: Howard Stark
characters.description: Tony's father: inventor, wartime industrialist, and a founder of S.H.I.E.L.D.

phases.phase-1:
Captain America: The First Avenger: the man who builds Steve's shield and flies him behind enemy lines.
Iron Man 2: the long game. The element Tony needs is hidden in the layout of the Stark Expo, decades early, with a film reel telling him he is the greatest thing Howard ever made.
phases.phase-3:
Ant-Man: 1989, taking Hank Pym's resignation to his face over the Pym Particle.
Captain America: Civil War: the tape of how he and Maria actually died in 1991, killed by the Winter Soldier on HYDRA's orders. It is what breaks Tony and Steve apart.
Avengers: Endgame: Tony meets him in 1970 without saying who he is, and gets a conversation with a father who is about to have a son.

characters.name: Wong
characters.description: Master of the mystic arts and keeper of Kamar-Taj's library, and eventually a good deal more than a sidekick.

phases.phase-3:
Doctor Strange: the librarian at Kamar-Taj who does not laugh at Strange's jokes and drills the rules into him.
Avengers: Infinity War: holds the line in the New York fight.
Avengers: Endgame: opens portals with the rest of them.
phases.phase-4:
Spider-Man: No Way Home: Sorcerer Supreme by now on a technicality, since Strange was dust for five years and seniority is seniority. He tells Peter no about the spell and leaves before it goes wrong.
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness: he holds Kamar-Taj against Wanda, and loses it.
phases.phase-5:
Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings: the cage match with Abomination, and the post-credits examination of the rings.
She-Hulk: Attorney at Law: a recurring guest, mostly to Jen's irritation.

characters.name: The Ancient One
characters.description: The enigmatic Sorcerer Supreme who takes Stephen Strange as a student.

phases.phase-3:
Doctor Strange: the teacher who opens his mind with one palm strike, and whose own secret is that she has stayed alive for centuries drawing on the Dark Dimension she forbids everyone else to touch. She dies stretching one second of lightning out into a conversation.
Avengers: Endgame: 2012, reluctantly handing Banner the Time Stone once he tells her Strange gave his up willingly.

characters.name: Christine Palmer
characters.description: An emergency surgeon at Metro-General, and Stephen Strange's former colleague and ex.

phases.phase-3: Doctor Strange: the one colleague who keeps showing up after the crash ends his career. She is the surgeon he goes to when nobody else will have him, she operates on him while his own astral form stands over her arguing about it, and she is the only person in the film who treats him as a man rather than as a problem to be solved. She also tells him plainly that he has always had to be the one holding the knife.
phases.phase-4: Multiverse of Madness: the version from this universe marries someone else, and Strange goes to the wedding and has to sit through it. The one who matters to the plot is the Christine Palmer of Earth-838, a scientist on that world's expedition team, who breaks Strange out of the Illuminati's cells and stays with him through the fight at Wundagore before going home to her own universe.

characters.name: Karl Mordo
characters.description: A devout master of Kamar-Taj and Strange's first ally in the mystic arts.

phases.phase-3: Doctor Strange: he recruits Strange off the street and fights beside him, until he learns the Ancient One fed on the darkness she banned and that Strange broke natural law to win. He walks away from Kamar-Taj having decided there are too many sorcerers, and the post-credits shows him starting to do something about it.
phases.phase-4: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness: the Mordo in this one is a different universe's variant, an Illuminati member who sentences Strange with a smile. The one from this universe is still out there somewhere.

characters.name: Heimdall
characters.description: The all-seeing guardian of Asgard's Bifrost bridge.

phases.phase-1: Thor: the gatekeeper who sees almost everything, and who lets Thor's friends through against orders rather than kneel to Loki.
phases.phase-2:
Thor: The Dark World: he takes down a cloaked ship with his bare hands, and commits treason with a clear conscience to get Thor to Malekith.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: he is in the vision Wanda puts in Thor's head, blind, telling him he has doomed them all.
phases.phase-3:
Thor: Ragnarok: running Asgard's refugees out of the mountains while Hela holds the city.
Avengers: Infinity War: his last act is spending the Bifrost's dark magic to send the Hulk to Earth as a warning. Thanos kills him for it.
phases.phase-5: Thor: Love and Thunder: he meets Jane at the doors of Valhalla in the tag, and his son Axl, who inherited a piece of the sight, helps Thor track Gorr.

characters.name: Odin
characters.description: All-Father of Asgard, whose long reign hides some old secrets.

phases.phase-1: Thor: he banishes his heir to teach him what arrogance costs, and the secret of Loki's adoption comes out on his watch.
phases.phase-2: Thor: The Dark World: grief over Frigga turns his judgement, and he would spend every Asgardian life to avenge her. He never notices the throne being taken out from under him at the end.
phases.phase-3: Thor: Ragnarok: found living out his exile quietly in Norway, and he dies forgiving both sons. His death is the lock coming off the cell. Hela is his firstborn, and the empire he built was built on her.

characters.name: Korg
characters.description: A soft-spoken gladiator made of rocks, with a gentle voice and a revolutionary streak.

phases.phase-3:
Thor: Ragnarok: Sakaar's friendliest gladiator, whose failed revolution finally works when he leads the uprising in the arena.
Avengers: Endgame: five years deep into Fortnite with Thor in New Asgard.
phases.phase-5: Thor: Love and Thunder: he narrates the film. Zeus shatters him down to a face on a pile of rocks, he recovers from it, and he ends up with another Kronan and an explanation nobody asked for about how the two of them have children.

characters.name: Hank Pym
characters.description: The original Ant-Man. A brilliant, prickly scientist guarding the secret of the Pym Particle.

phases.phase-3:
Ant-Man: the Cold War's shrinking operative, who resigned rather than hand the particle over and lost Janet to the Quantum Realm decades ago. He recruits a burglar rather than let Darren Cross weaponise the work, and rather than risk Hope doing it.
Ant-Man and the Wasp: he builds the tunnel, goes down himself, and brings Janet back. Then dusts in the credits scene standing next to her.
Avengers: Endgame: restored with everyone else.
phases.phase-4: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania: pulled under with the rest of the family, where he learns what Janet never told any of them. His ant colony, evolved centuries ahead in the time dilation down there, arrives as the cavalry.

characters.name: Janet van Dyne
characters.description: Hank's wife and the original Wasp, lost to the Quantum Realm decades ago.

phases.phase-3:
Ant-Man: the 1987 flashback, going subatomic to disarm a missile and not coming back out.
Ant-Man and the Wasp: found alive after thirty years down there, changed by it, and briefly able to speak through Scott. She dusts in the car park minutes after getting home.
Avengers: Endgame: restored with everyone else.
phases.phase-4: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania: her thirty years finally get explained. She survived down there, met a stranded traveller, repaired the multiversal core of his ship, and worked out what he actually was in time to strand him. She is the reason Kang was trapped, and the reason the family has any idea how to fight him.

characters.name: Luis
characters.description: Scott's ex-cellmate and business partner, teller of the MCU's most elaborate secondhand stories.

phases.phase-3:
Ant-Man: Scott's cellmate turned crewmate, and the source of the tip that starts the whole job. The way he relays a story is the best running gag in either film.
Ant-Man and the Wasp: co-founder of X-Con Security, and dosed with truth serum at exactly the wrong moment, which produces a full account of Scott's love life for men who only wanted an address.

characters.name: Okoye
characters.description: General of the Dora Milaje, Wakanda's elite royal guard, and the definition of loyalty.

phases.phase-3:
Black Panther: general of the Dora Milaje, loyal to the throne even when Killmonger is sitting on it, and she only turns when he goes after the thing the throne exists to protect. The post-credits has Bucky waking up in a Wakandan village, deprogrammed.
Avengers: Infinity War: on the field at the Battle of Wakanda.
Avengers: Endgame: back through the portals.
phases.phase-5: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: beaten by Namor and stripped of her rank for losing Shuri, she goes back into the fight out of uniform, in the Midnight Angel armour.

characters.name: Shuri
characters.description: T'Challa's little sister and Wakanda's smartest scientist.

phases.phase-3:
Black Panther: sixteen, running the most advanced lab on the planet, and merciless about her brother's sandals. The Bucky she deprograms between films is her work too.
Avengers: Infinity War: racing to get the Mind Stone out of Vision's head, and very nearly getting there.
Avengers: Endgame: back for the final battle.
phases.phase-5: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: she fails to save T'Challa, loses her mother to Namor's attack, synthesises the heart-shaped herb from a Talokanil flower, and takes the mantle fully intending to use it for revenge. She stops at the edge of it. The last thing she does is burn the funeral robes on a beach in Haiti.

characters.name: Nakia
characters.description: A Wakandan spy and T'Challa's former love, who believes Wakanda should open up and help the world.

phases.phase-3: Black Panther: a War Dog who would rather be freeing trafficking victims than guarding a border, and the argument for engagement that T'Challa eventually adopts as policy. She is the one who steals the last heart-shaped herb that saves him.
phases.phase-5: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: living quietly in Haiti until Ramonda calls in the one operative she still trusts, and she gets Shuri out of Talokan. The ending explains the distance. She has been raising T'Challa's son.

characters.name: M'Baku
characters.description: Leader of Wakanda's mountain-dwelling Jabari tribe, and a rival with his own strict code of honour.

phases.phase-3:
Black Panther: he challenges T'Challa at the waterfall and loses, then shelters the royal family and marches the Jabari into a war he could have sat out.
Avengers: Infinity War: on the line at the Battle of Wakanda.
Avengers: Endgame: back through the portals.
phases.phase-5: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: the loudest realist on the war council, and the one who says the unwelcome thing to Shuri about what revenge is going to cost her. The film ends with him walking into the challenge circle.

characters.name: Ramonda
characters.description: Queen mother of Wakanda.

phases.phase-3: Black Panther: the steel behind the throne through the coronation and Killmonger's coup, and she flees to the Jabari with the last of the herb.
phases.phase-5: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: a queen who has buried her husband and her son and still faces down the UN over it. She strips Okoye of her rank to protect Shuri, and she drowns saving Riri when Namor floods the throne room. Her death is what pushes Shuri towards the herb.

characters.name: Ayo
characters.description: A senior member of the Dora Milaje, Wakanda's royal guard, who has stood post for T'Chaka, T'Challa and Ramonda in turn.

phases.phase-3:
Captain America: Civil War: on T'Chaka's detail in Vienna, and the one who tells Black Widow to move or be moved.
Black Panther: in the Dora line through the coronation, Killmonger's challenge and the fight that follows.
Avengers: Infinity War: holding the line at the Battle of Wakanda.
Avengers: Endgame: back through the portals for the last fight.
phases.phase-4: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: she leads the Dora detail that comes for Zemo, and she has a claim on him. She spent years in Wakanda undoing what Hydra did to Bucky's head, and she tests it by speaking the trigger words to his face. When John Walker will not hand the shield over, she and the Dora take him apart in about a minute. She is also the one who delivers the Wakandan-made suit at the end.
phases.phase-5: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: she covers for Aneka after the prototype armour is used without permission, which is what costs Okoye her rank. Shuri gives the two of them the Midnight Angel suits for the war with Talokan.

characters.name: Everett Ross
characters.description: A sharp CIA agent who keeps finding himself tangled up in Wakandan affairs.

phases.phase-3:
Captain America: Civil War: the bureaucrat holding Zemo's leash, briefly.
Black Panther: he takes a bullet for Nakia, gets put back together by Shuri's lab, and flies the remote dogfight that stops the vibranium shipments leaving.
phases.phase-5: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: feeding Wakanda intelligence against his own agency, which his ex-wife, Director Valentina Allegra de Fontaine, arrests him for. Wakanda returns the favour with a jailbreak.

characters.name: Michelle "MJ" Jones
characters.description: Peter Parker's sardonic classmate, and far too observant for anyone's good.

phases.phase-3: Spider-Man: Homecoming: deadpan, in the background of most of it, and reading a book at every decathlon meet.
phases.phase-4:
Spider-Man: Far From Home: she has already worked out who he is by watching him, and their first real moment together is him confirming it.
Spider-Man: No Way Home: his anchor through the whole mess, and the one who catches the detail everybody else misses. Then the spell takes him from her, and Peter decides not to introduce himself again.

characters.name: Ned Leeds
characters.description: Peter's best friend and dedicated "guy in the chair."

phases.phase-3: Spider-Man: Homecoming: he finds Spider-Man in his bedroom halfway through a LEGO Death Star, and appoints himself mission control.
phases.phase-4:
Spider-Man: Far From Home: a summer romance with Betty Brant conducted entirely at superhero-plot-adjacent volume.
Spider-Man: No Way Home: it turns out he can use a sling ring first try. He pulls two other Peter Parkers out of the multiverse by accident, makes them promise the best-friend-betrays-you thing is not going to happen to him, and then forgets Peter ever existed.

characters.name: May Parker
characters.description: Peter's aunt, guardian, and moral compass.

phases.phase-3:
Captain America: Civil War: Tony turns up in her flat to recruit Peter, and she has no idea what she is being lied to about.
Spider-Man: Homecoming: it ends on her walking in on the suit.
phases.phase-4:
Spider-Man: Far From Home: running a charity for people displaced by the Blip, in on the secret at last, and flirting with Happy.
Spider-Man: No Way Home: she is the conscience of the film. Curing the villains rather than sending them back to die is her call, the Green Goblin kills her for it, and she gives Peter the line about power and responsibility before she goes.

characters.name: Darcy Lewis
characters.description: Jane Foster's snarky intern, eventually a doctor of astrophysics in her own right.

phases.phase-1: Thor: the political science intern who tases the God of Thunder in a car park and insists on calling Mjolnir Mew-Mew.
phases.phase-2: Thor: The Dark World: she has acquired an intern of her own by now, and keeps the science running while Jane is otherwise occupied.
phases.phase-4: WandaVision: Doctor Lewis now, and the astrophysicist who works out that the Hex is broadcasting a sitcom. She watches Westview the way the audience does, names the episodes, and drives a funnel-cake truck through the finale.

characters.name: Jimmy Woo
characters.description: An earnest FBI agent with close-up magic aspirations.

phases.phase-3: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Scott's house-arrest handler, always about thirty seconds behind him, learning card tricks out of professional spite.
phases.phase-4: WandaVision: the missing-persons case that cracks Westview open is his, the card trick is flawless by now, and the whiteboard of questions is where the investigation actually starts.

characters.name: Talos
characters.description: A commander of the shapeshifting alien Skrulls.

phases.phase-3: Captain Marvel: the sinister shapeshifting general turns out to be a refugee commander looking for his hidden family and Mar-Vell's engine. The Skrulls were the ones being hunted the whole time.
phases.phase-4: Spider-Man: Far From Home: the tag reveals he spent the entire film being Nick Fury, glasses and growl included, while the real one was off-world.
phases.phase-5: Secret Invasion: thirty years of promises later, the Skrulls who gave up waiting follow Gravik instead. Talos stays loyal to both species and Gravik kills him for it. His daughter G'iah inherits the fight.

characters.name: Katy Chen
characters.description: Shang-Chi's best friend, dragged from parking cars into world-saving.

phases.phase-5: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings: ten years of karaoke and valet shifts with a best friend she thought she knew, until one bus fight rewrites all of it. In Ta Lo she picks up a bow, trains for roughly a day, and still puts the arrow where it needs to go. She ends the film name-dropping dragons at brunch, about ten seconds before Wong portals them both away.

characters.name: Xu Xialing
characters.description: Shang-Chi's estranged sister, self-taught because no one would train her.

phases.phase-5: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings: abandoned twice over, by the brother who ran and the father who only ever saw a son, so she built her own underground fight empire out of nothing. She fights for Ta Lo, buries her father, and then takes his chair. The credits scene has her running the Ten Rings, remade the way she wants them.

characters.name: Alexei Shostakov / Red Guardian
characters.description: Russia's washed-up super soldier answer to Captain America. Loud, proud, and well past his prime.

phases.phase-3: Black Widow: the fake American father of the Ohio operation, and by the present day a gulag lifer telling embellished stories about the time he fought Captain America. His daughters break him out. He is comic relief and genuine wreckage in the same scene, a man who loved a fake family more than the state that assigned it to him.
phases.phase-6: Thunderbolts*: driving a limo and clipping out Yelena's news mentions. Valentina's mess hands him one more chance to matter and he takes it with both hands, and appoints himself a founding member of the New Avengers.

characters.name: Melina Vostokoff
characters.description: A veteran Black Widow and brilliant scientist from Natasha's fake childhood family.

phases.phase-3: Black Widow: the fake mother of the Ohio operation, and the scientist whose pheromone-lock work is what cages the next generation of Widows. The reunion forces her to look at what she built. She switches sides, fakes Dreykov out with a face swap, and brings the Red Room down from the inside.

characters.name: Layla El-Faouly
characters.description: An adventurer and archaeologist tangled up in Marc Spector's past.

phases.phase-5: Moon Knight: Marc's estranged wife, who married a man without knowing there were two of him, and whose father's death is the thing between them. In the finale she takes on the goddess Taweret as a temporary avatar, golden wings over Cairo, and a small girl asks her whether she is an Egyptian superhero.

characters.name: Mobius
characters.description: A TVA analyst with a soft spot for jet skis and a knack for getting under Loki's skin.

phases.phase-4:
Loki: Season 1: the analyst who would rather interview a Loki than prune one, and whose faith in this particular variant bends the whole organisation out of shape. Renslayer prunes him for asking where his own file came from.
Loki: Season 2: he learns what his life was before the TVA took it, goes to look at it, and does not knock on the door. He resigns once the crisis is over and drives out to watch his sons from across the road.

characters.name: Sylvie
characters.description: A dangerous fugitive variant with a lifelong grudge against the TVA.

phases.phase-4:
Loki: Season 1: taken by the TVA as a child for the crime of existing, and she grew up hiding inside apocalypses and enchanting her way towards revenge. The season ends with her kissing Loki, shoving him back through a time door, and running He Who Remains through, which is what breaks the multiverse open.
Loki: Season 2: working a McDonald's in 1982 Oklahoma and defending her right to have a life rather than a purpose. She is still there swinging when the Loom crisis needs her.

characters.name: Hunter B-15
characters.description: The TVA hunter who leads the field teams that arrest variants off the timeline.

phases.phase-4:
Loki: Season 1: the hunter who arrests Loki in the Gobi Desert in the first episode, and for most of the season the TVA's blunt instrument. Sylvie enchants her during the hurricane in Alabama, and what B-15 sees inside her own head while it is happening starts the crack. She is the one who takes Loki and Sylvie to the Time-Keepers, and she is standing there when the three rulers of the organisation turn out to be androids with nobody behind them.
