Loki: Season 2: running what is left of the place from the inside, and arguing that the workforce deserve to be told they were all people before they were taken. She comes out of the Loom crisis promoted into one of the senior roles at the TVA.
Deadpool & Wolverine: she turns up again at the end, when the TVA arrive to arrest Paradox.

characters.name: Ravonna Renslayer
characters.description: A TVA judge who sentences variants for stepping off the Sacred Timeline, and one of the organisation's true believers.

phases.phase-4:
Loki: Season 1: the judge who sentences Loki to be reset in the first episode, and the closest thing the TVA has to a true believer. She was a hunter long before she was a judge, and the flashback to Sylvie's arrest as a child on Asgard is her. She prunes Mobius when he starts reading his own file, and she prunes Loki in the Time-Keepers' chamber. Finding out the Time-Keepers are hollow does not break her, it just makes her want to know who is really in charge.
Loki: Season 2: chasing that answer alongside Miss Minutes and what He Who Remains left behind. Sylvie prunes her, and it ends with her in the Void with Alioth coming.

characters.name: Isaiah Bradley
characters.description: A Black super-soldier from the Korean War era, erased from history.

phases.phase-4: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: the government's secret Korean War super soldier, rewarded with thirty years of imprisonment and experimentation and then erased from the record. His story nearly convinces Sam to drop the shield. Instead Sam makes the country look at him, and puts Isaiah's statue in the Smithsonian next to Steve's exhibit.
phases.phase-6: Captain America: Brave New World: mind-controlled by Sterns into an assassination attempt on President Ross, which is the frame job the film runs on. Sam clears him, but not before he is back in a cell for it.

characters.name: Joaquin Torres
characters.description: An Air Force first lieutenant stationed in Tunisia, and Sam Wilson's man on the ground for intelligence.

phases.phase-4: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: Sam's Air Force liaison, flying support on the hostage rescue over Tunisia and running down leads on the Flag Smashers afterwards. He walks into one of their meetings in Munich on his own and gets a broken nose out of it, then keeps feeding Sam names and locations for the rest of the series. By the end he has Sam's wrecked EXO-7 wings in his hands and a standing offer to fly as Sam's wingman.
phases.phase-6: Brave New World: the new Falcon, in the wings and beside Sam from the opening raid in Mexico to take back a stolen adamantium sample. He is in the room when the assassination attempt goes off at the White House, and he is shot down over the Indian Ocean when the Japanese fleet opens fire during the standoff at Celestial Island. Sam gets him out of the water alive, and he spends the last stretch of the film in a hospital bed.

characters.name: Jack Duquesne
characters.description: A master fencer and old-money socialite, engaged to Kate Bishop's mother Eleanor.

phases.phase-4: Hawkeye introduces him as Eleanor Bishop's fiancé and spends five episodes pointing at him. He is a genuinely dangerous swordsman with a collection of blades, one of which matches the wound that kills his uncle Armand Duquesne, and Kate is certain he is behind everything happening to her family. He is not. Eleanor had installed him as CEO of Sloan Limited, the company laundering money for the Tracksuit Mafia, and on Christmas Eve he is arrested over it while Eleanor is arrested for Armand's murder.
phases.phase-6: Daredevil: Born Again brings him back as the vigilante Swordsman.

characters.name: Sersi
characters.description: An Eternal who genuinely loves humanity, living quietly in London until her people's past resurfaces.

phases.phase-5: Eternals: the matter-transmuter who chose museum work and a human boyfriend over cosmic purpose. Ajak's death makes her the reluctant Prime Eternal, and finding out what they actually are, machines shepherding a Celestial birth that will break the planet open, makes her the one who refuses it. She turns the emerging Tiamut to marble mid-birth, and Arishem pulls her off Earth for judgement in the tag.

characters.name: Ikaris
characters.description: The most powerful of the Eternals, with flight, enormous strength and eye-beams to match.

phases.phase-5: Eternals: the loyal soldier of the group, loyal it turns out to Arishem rather than to Earth. He fed Ajak to the Deviants to keep the emergence on schedule, fights his own family over it, and, unable to kill Sersi or live with what he has done, flies into the sun.

characters.name: Ajak
characters.description: The Eternals' healer and leader, their only bridge to their creators.

phases.phase-5: Eternals: the Prime Eternal, five thousand years into midwifing a civilisation, who chose Earth over Arishem once the population rebound after Endgame put the emergence back on schedule. Ikaris killed her for it before the film's first act, and the mystery of her death is the thread the family pulls.

characters.name: Thena
characters.description: The Eternals' greatest warrior, haunted by memories she shouldn't have.

phases.phase-5: Eternals: her Mahd Wy'ry is not madness. It is leakage from previous emergences, every erased planet's worth of memory their masters kept wiping. Gilgamesh spent centuries steadying her, and after his death she fights through the fog and kills the Deviant that took him. She leaves aboard the Domo with Druig and Makkari to warn other Eternals.

characters.name: Kingo
characters.description: An Eternal hiding in plain sight as a century-spanning dynasty of Bollywood stars, all of whom are him.

phases.phase-5: Eternals: he arrives at the apocalypse with a one-man documentary crew in tow. When the family splits over whether to let Earth die he takes the option nobody respects, which is that he will not fight his family and will not fight for Arishem either, so he leaves.

characters.name: Agatha Harkness
characters.description: A centuries-old witch with a talent for showing up wherever the magic is.

phases.phase-4:
WandaVision: the nosy neighbour Agnes is a Salem-era witch who has been picking at Wanda's grief to work out how she casts. Wanda drains her and leaves her locked inside the Agnes persona.
Agatha All Along: sprung from that spell by a teenage boy who will not give his name, she cons a scratch coven onto the Witches' Road. There is no Road. It is a song her son Nicholas Scratch wrote, which she has used for three centuries to walk covens somewhere quiet and drain them. The boy is Billy Maximoff, Rio Vidal is Death, and Agatha dies and carries on as a ghost only Billy can see.

characters.name: Wilson Fisk / Kingpin
characters.description: New York's brutal, immaculately dressed crime boss.

phases.phase-4:
Hawkeye: the power behind the Tracksuits, Eleanor Bishop's employer, and uncle to Maya Lopez, whose father he had killed to shape her. The finale ends with Maya's gun going off out of frame.
Echo: he survived it, one eye down, and comes to Tamaha in person to get her back. The series fills in the boy with the hammer who became the Kingpin. Maya reaches him through the ancestral connection and leaves him scrambled, and the last scene points him at a mayoral race.

characters.name: Wade Wilson / Deadpool
characters.description: A fourth-wall-demolishing mercenary with a healing factor and absolutely no filter.

phases.phase-4: Deadpool & Wolverine: pulled out of retirement, and out of a car dealership, by the TVA telling him his universe is dying because its anchor being is dead. His plan is to go and find a replacement Wolverine. One trip through the Void, one Cassandra Nova problem and several hundred crimes against the fourth wall later, he saves his timeline and the people in it, and lands in the MCU while mocking it from the inside.

characters.name: Logan / Wolverine
characters.description: A clawed, near-unkillable mutant with a very long list of regrets.

phases.phase-4: Deadpool & Wolverine: not the Logan who died at the end of that film. This is the one who was not there when his X-Men were killed, drinking his way across the multiverse in a yellow suit he does not think he has earned. Wade drags him into being the anchor his own world lost, and by the end it fits. He stays on Earth-10005 afterwards, as Wade's flatmate, to the horror of both of them.

characters.name: Reed Richards / Mister Fantastic
characters.description: The smartest man of his world. An elastic scientist leading Earth's first family of heroes.

phases.phase-4: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness: a variant only. The Illuminati's Reed explains exactly how dangerous Wanda is, shortly before she demonstrates it on him.
phases.phase-6: The Fantastic Four: First Steps: on Earth-828, four years into being his world's first family, Reed hits the problem he cannot out-think. Galactus wants his newborn son Franklin as the price of sparing Earth. He refuses the trade, turns a planet's worth of panic into a plan, and helps put the Devourer through a teleport portal. The tag moves the family to the main universe.

characters.name: Sue Storm / Invisible Woman
characters.description: Scientist and diplomat with invisibility and force fields; the family's center of gravity.

phases.phase-6: The Fantastic Four: First Steps: pregnant through the first act and delivering Franklin in zero gravity mid-escape from Galactus. She is the one who rallies a frightened planet into standing together rather than handing the child over. In the climax she puts everything she has into shoving Galactus through the portal and dies doing it, and Franklin brings her back.

characters.name: Johnny Storm / Human Torch
characters.description: Sue's hotheaded (literally) pilot brother.

phases.phase-6: The Fantastic Four: First Steps: he takes the Silver Surfer personally, obsesses over her broadcasts, decodes her language, and works out that the herald was a person who traded herself to save her own world. Talking to her in that language is what breaks her loyalty to Galactus.

characters.name: Ben Grimm / The Thing
characters.description: The Fantastic Four's rock-skinned strongman with the softest heart on the team.

phases.phase-6: The Fantastic Four: First Steps: the pilot who paid for the cosmic rays with his skin, and by now Earth-828's favourite uncle. Yancy Street's own, quietly courting a schoolteacher, and first through every wall when Galactus arrives.

characters.name: Silver Surfer
characters.description: A chrome-skinned herald riding ahead of something world-ending.

phases.phase-6: The Fantastic Four: First Steps: Shalla-Bal, the herald who marks Earth for her master, and who was once a person who gave herself to Galactus to spare her own world. Johnny refusing to treat her as a monster, in her own language, is what turns her, and she breaks from Galactus when it counts.

characters.name: Thanos
characters.description: The Mad Titan, a warlord pursuing all six Infinity Stones with a terrifying sense of purpose.

phases.phase-1: The Avengers: the credits scene turns the whole invasion into a job interview. The figure behind Loki's army turns around and smiles at the words about courting Death.
phases.phase-2:
Guardians of the Galaxy: holding court as Ronan's patron and the father Gamora and Nebula were raised by, until Ronan decides to keep the stone for himself.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: the tag is him deciding he is finished delegating.
phases.phase-3:
Avengers: Infinity War: effectively the protagonist. Six stones in two days, the only thing he loves traded away on Vormir, and he wins.
Avengers: Endgame: it kills him twice. The broken farmer Thor beheads in the first twenty minutes, and then the 2014 version who comes forward for a second attempt and dusts mid-sentence.

characters.name: Ultron
characters.description: Tony Stark's peacekeeping AI gone horribly right: it looked at the data and decided humanity was the threat.

phases.phase-2: Avengers: Age of Ultron: alive for a matter of minutes before concluding that peace in our time requires extinction. He builds a body, an army, a city he intends to drop on the planet, and a philosophy, quoting Pinocchio the whole way through. The perfect body he built for himself wakes up as the Vision instead, and it is the Vision who switches the last of him off, almost gently.

characters.name: Hela
characters.description: The Goddess of Death, whose return spells doom for Asgard.

phases.phase-3: Thor: Ragnarok: Odin's firstborn and his original executioner, painted over in the palace murals along with everything the two of them did together. Released by his death, she catches Mjolnir and crushes it, takes Asgard in an afternoon, and can only be stopped by the apocalypse itself. Thor starts Ragnarok deliberately and Surtur brings the kingdom down on her.

characters.name: Red Skull
characters.description: Head of HYDRA, the Nazi deep-science division, and the first super-soldier experiment gone wrong.

phases.phase-1: Captain America: The First Avenger: Erskine's formula in an unworthy man. Johann Schmidt takes HYDRA private and sets out to out-do the people he works for. Grabbing the Tesseract bare-handed does not kill him, it relocates him.
phases.phase-3:
Avengers: Infinity War: Vormir answers where to. He is the Soul Stone's keeper, cursed to guide people to a thing he can never hold, and he watches Thanos work out the price.
Avengers: Endgame: he is still there when Natasha and Clint arrive to have the same argument.

characters.name: Helmut Zemo
characters.description: A meticulous Sokovian mastermind who despises what super-people cost the world.

phases.phase-3: Captain America: Civil War: no powers and no army, just patience. A Sokovian colonel who lost his family under Ultron's meteor, he frames Bucky, digs up one buried tape, and splits the Avengers with the truth on it. His plan works exactly as intended.
phases.phase-4: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: broken out for the Flag Smasher hunt, and he brings a purple mask, a Sokovian fortune and a dance. He is still convinced super soldiers are a mistake, and the series does not entirely disagree with him. The Dora Milaje take him to the Raft at the end.

characters.name: Erik Killmonger
characters.description: A black-ops soldier with a righteous grievance and a claim on Wakanda's throne.

phases.phase-3: Black Panther: N'Jadaka, the cousin Wakanda left in Oakland after T'Chaka killed his father. He wins the throne fairly under Wakandan law, which is the sting of it, and his plan is his father's dream turned into a weapon: vibranium to every oppressed people on Earth. T'Challa beats the man and keeps the question.
phases.phase-5: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: waiting on the ancestral plane when Shuri burns the herb, and asking her whether she intends to be her brother or him.

characters.name: Ulysses Klaue
characters.description: A cackling arms dealer and one of the only outsiders to have seen the real Wakanda.

phases.phase-2: Avengers: Age of Ultron: the black-market source of the stolen vibranium, paid in billions and one severed arm for comparing Ultron to Stark.
phases.phase-3: Black Panther: a sonic cannon where the arm used to be, and the only outsider who knows what Wakanda actually is. Killmonger uses him as an entry ticket, since a Wakandan needs a body to present at the border.

characters.name: Adrian Toomes / Vulture
characters.description: A blue-collar salvager turned winged, high-tech arms dealer.

phases.phase-3: Spider-Man: Homecoming: a salvage contractor squeezed out of the Chitauri clean-up by Damage Control, who kept what he had already lifted and built a weapons business out of it. The car ride, where he works out who Peter is while driving him to a school dance, is the best scene in the film. He goes to prison and keeps the name to himself.

characters.name: Quentin Beck / Mysterio
characters.description: A caped hero who claims to have come from another Earth.

phases.phase-4: Spider-Man: Far From Home: the man from another Earth is a fired Stark illusion engineer with drones, projectors, and a support group of other people Tony annoyed. He plays mentor to a grieving Peter to get EDITH off him, very nearly pulls it off, and turns his own death into the last move. The doctored footage names Peter and pins a murder on him.

characters.name: Xu Wenwu
characters.description: The immortal holder of the Ten Rings, leader of the criminal empire named for them, and Shang-Chi's father.

phases.phase-5: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings: a thousand years of conquest, and one decade of retirement for a woman who could beat him. When Li died the rings went back on and the children got an assassin's education instead of a childhood. What he becomes is grief with resources. The thing behind the gate in Ta Lo speaks with his wife's voice, and he tears the gate open to reach her. His last act is putting the rings on his son.

characters.name: Gorr the God Butcher
characters.description: A grieving zealot armed with a god-killing blade.

phases.phase-5: Thor: Love and Thunder: the last believer on a dead world, whose god laughed at his daughter's grave, which is what the Necrosword had been waiting for. His crusade drags Thor through kidnapped children and a shadow realm to Eternity's altar, where he gets one wish and spends it on his daughter rather than on killing gods. Thor raises her.

characters.name: Namor
characters.description: The winged-ankled king of a hidden undersea civilization.

phases.phase-5: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: K'uk'ulkan, a centuries-old mutant born out of the same vibranium desperation that hid Wakanda, ruling Talokan under the ocean. The surface world hunting vibranium is what makes him strike first, and he floods Wakanda's capital and kills its queen. Shuri beats him and spares him, and his last scene suggests he took the concession as strategy.

characters.name: Kang
characters.description: A conqueror with mastery over time, and countless variants of himself scattered across the multiverse.

phases.phase-4:
Loki: Season 1: the original. He Who Remains, the variant who won the war against his own kind and pruned every timeline but one to stop them coming back. Sylvie kills him and lets all of them out.
Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania: Kang the Conqueror, the variant Janet met and stranded, who erases timelines for a living and is beaten in the Quantum Realm by ants and Langs. The mid-credits fills an arena with thousands more of him.
Loki: Season 2: Victor Timely, a nineteenth-century inventor with the same face and none of the menace.

characters.name: Alioth
characters.description: A living storm the size of a weather front that grazes at the end of time and consumes whatever it finds there.

phases.phase-4:
Loki: Season 1: the thing patrolling the Void, the wasteland where everything the TVA prunes gets dumped rather than destroyed. Sylvie works out it is not a scavenger but a guard, which is the clue that something worth guarding sits behind it, and she and Loki only get through by enchanting it together.
Deadpool & Wolverine: most of the film takes place in that same Void, where Alioth is still the apex predator and Cassandra Nova uses it to dispose of anyone she has finished with.

characters.name: The High Evolutionary
characters.description: A god-playing scientist obsessed with engineering a perfect society, no matter the cost.

phases.phase-5: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3: the Sovereign's creator, Counter-Earth's landlord, and the man who built Rocket one cage and one dead friend at a time, then labelled him property when the experiment turned out cleverer than its maker. The film gives him no tragic backstory at all. Rocket leaves him alive and finished.

characters.name: Taskmaster
characters.description: A masked operative who can perfectly mimic any fighting style after seeing it once.

phases.phase-3: Black Widow: the Red Room's mirror fighter, and its worst secret. Under the mask is Antonia Dreykov, the daughter Natasha's defection maimed, rebuilt by her father into something that copies any fighter it watches. The antidote frees her along with the rest of the Widows.
phases.phase-6: Thunderbolts*: recruited into Valentina's containment-room clean-up, and killed in the opening crossfire.

characters.name: Darren Cross / Yellowjacket
characters.description: Hank Pym's former protégé at Pym Technologies, and the man who pushed him out of his own company.

phases.phase-3: Ant-Man: Hank's protégé turned successor, running Pym Technologies after forcing Hank off his own board, and obsessed with recreating the Pym Particle Hank refused to hand over. He gets there eventually and builds the Yellowjacket suit, a weaponised version he intends to sell. The instability he never solved is what finishes him. During the fight with Scott in Cassie's bedroom, Scott gets inside the suit and sabotages the regulator, and Cross shrinks uncontrollably until there is nothing left of him.
phases.phase-4: Quantumania: he did not die. Shrinking out of control dropped him into the Quantum Realm, where Kang found what was left and rebuilt it into MODOK, a Mechanized Organism Designed Only for Killing, which in practice is Cross's face on an enormous head bolted to a small armoured body. He works as Kang's hunter until Cassie Lang tells him he does not have to be a weapon, and he turns on Kang in the final fight and is killed doing it.

characters.name: Ava Starr / Ghost
characters.description: A woman phasing painfully in and out of solid reality thanks to a childhood quantum accident.

phases.phase-3: Ant-Man and the Wasp: the lab accident that killed her parents left her phasing in and out of solid matter and in constant pain, and S.H.I.E.L.D. turned the condition into a stealth asset before discarding her. She goes after the Pyms' tunnel for relief rather than power, and Janet's returned energy steadies her.
phases.phase-6: Thunderbolts*: phasing more reliably now and on Valentina's payroll, until the containment-room trap. She walks out a founding New Avenger, which surprises her more than anyone.

characters.name: Emil Blonsky / Abomination
characters.description: A soldier whose super serum experiment went monstrous, and who later tries, sincerely or not, to reform.

phases.phase-1: The Incredible Hulk: a career commando who chases the Hulk's power through Ross's serum and Banner's blood until he becomes the Abomination, and wrecks Harlem before the Hulk chokes him out.
phases.phase-5:
Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings: cage-fighting Wong, with whom he appears to have an arrangement.
She-Hulk: Attorney at Law: Jen's client at his parole hearing, running a wellness retreat with seven soul mates. The reform is largely genuine. The paid Abomination appearances breaking his parole are also real, and he goes back to the Raft.

characters.name: Thaddeus Ross
characters.description: The hard-line general who hunted the Hulk, whose political career keeps on climbing.

phases.phase-1: The Incredible Hulk: the general who made Banner a fugitive, and whose daughter Betty loved him anyway. His serum programme is what produces the Abomination.
phases.phase-3:
Captain America: Civil War: Secretary of State by now, delivering the Accords ultimatum and jailing half the team when they refuse it.
Black Widow: still hunting fugitives, and still a step behind Natasha.
Avengers: Infinity War: on a screen from Washington, being ignored.
Avengers: Endgame: at Tony's funeral.
phases.phase-6: Captain America: Brave New World: President Ross, trying to be better than his own record, while Samuel Sterns, the gamma scientist he has had locked up and exploited for years, takes it apart from the inside. The pills keeping Ross alive turn him into the Red Hulk on live television. He ends the film resigned, imprisoned, and talking to Betty.

characters.name: Valentina Allegra de Fontaine
characters.description: A silky Washington power broker quietly recruiting "assets" for purposes unknown.

phases.phase-3: Black Widow: the credits scene, at Natasha's grave, handing Yelena a photograph of Clint Barton.
phases.phase-4: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: she appears beside a court-martialled John Walker with a card that has not been printed yet, and the title U.S. Agent.
phases.phase-5: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: the day job, which is Director of the CIA. She is also Everett Ross's ex-wife, and she arrests him personally.
phases.phase-6: Thunderbolts*: the containment-room trap was her shredding evidence with the personnel still inside it. When the survivors walk out alive with Bob, she turns a press conference around mid-sentence and introduces the New Avengers.

characters.name: Erik Selvig
characters.description: An astrophysicist, Jane Foster's mentor, and one of the first scientists on Earth to treat Asgard as a physics problem rather than a myth.

phases.phase-1:
Thor: a colleague of Jane's father who thinks her Einstein-Rosen bridge research is a career-ender, right up until a man falls out of the sky. He is the one who gets Thor out of S.H.I.E.L.D. custody, and by the mid-credits Loki is already standing behind him, telling him what to say about the Tesseract.

The Avengers: taken by Loki in the opening scene and put under the sceptre's control. He is the reason the portal works, having built the device that stabilises the Tesseract on top of Stark Tower, and also the reason it can be closed, because he built in a failsafe while he was under and left Loki's own sceptre as the way to shut it. He is snapped out of it when Selvig is knocked unconscious.
phases.phase-2: Thor: The Dark World: has not recovered from being used. He was institutionalised after New York and turns up lecturing at Stonehenge with no trousers on, which the film plays for laughs and then quietly takes seriously. His gravimetric spikes are what let them fight through the Convergence at all, and they are the closest thing anyone has to a working theory of the nine realms.
phases.phase-4: He stops appearing after Phase Three, but his work does not stop being used. Spider-Man: Far From Home refers back to him, which is the point at which his research has outlived his own involvement in it.
phases.phase-5: Ms. Marvel: name-checked again by Bruno, Kamala's friend, in a scientific context. Two mentions across two phases, from characters with no connection to each other, which is a reasonable measure of how much of Earth's understanding of this stuff started with him.

characters.name: Dane Whitman
characters.description: A history professor at the Natural History Museum in London, and the closest thing Sersi has to a normal life.

phases.phase-5: Eternals: Sersi's boyfriend, kept outside the plot for most of the film and told the truth about her only once there's no way around it. He takes it about as well as anyone could. The post-credits scene is the point of him: he opens an old case containing the Ebony Blade, a sword with his family name on it, and an unseen voice asks whether he's sure he's ready for that. Nothing has been done with him since.

characters.name: Eros / Starfox
characters.description: A Titan-born Eternal with more charm than sense, who turns up looking for the members of the team who went missing.

phases.phase-5: Eternals: arrives in the mid-credits aboard Ted the ship, introduced by Pip the Troll as the prince of Titan and Thanos's brother. He tells the remaining Eternals he knows where their captured friends have been taken and offers to help get them back. That thread has not been picked up since.

characters.name: Khonshu
characters.description: The Egyptian god of the moon, who speaks through a chosen avatar and is only ever heard by the person he has chosen.

phases.phase-5: Moon Knight: the voice in Marc Spector's head and the source of his powers, kept alive by a bargain Marc made when he was dying. Khonshu wants wrongdoers punished, and the other gods have no patience for how he goes about it, so they seal him in stone partway through. He is not a benevolent patron. He picked Marc partly because a fractured mind is easier to steer, he threatens to take Layla as a replacement, and the final scene reveals he kept a third personality, Jake Lockley, as his own avatar the whole time, doing the killing Marc refused to do.

characters.name: Victor Timely
characters.description: An inventor and showman at the turn of the twentieth century, selling machines that are far too advanced for the year he's selling them in.

phases.phase-4:
Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania: the post-credits, lecturing a small crowd in 1901 while Loki and Mobius watch from the back of the room.
Loki: Season 2: a variant of He Who Remains, working from a technical manual Ravonna Renslayer and Miss Minutes handed him as a child, which makes him the only person alive who can repair the Temporal Loom. He is nervous, decent and badly out of his depth, and temporal radiation kills him on the gangway before he can finish.

characters.name: Bob Reynolds / Sentry
characters.description: A quiet man with a history of addiction and depression, who volunteered for something he didn't understand.

phases.phase-6: Thunderbolts*: Valentina's real project, and the reason she wanted the rest of the team dead. Bob was a test subject in a programme meant to reproduce the super-soldier serum, and it worked far past anyone's intention, leaving him with something close to unlimited power. The problem is that it came with the depression rather than instead of it. His low is a separate thing called the Void, which blacks out Manhattan and pulls people into their own worst memories, and it can't be fought, only talked down. The team reaches him rather than beating him, which is the whole argument of the film.

characters.name: John Walker
characters.description: The government's hand-picked replacement Captain America, and a decorated soldier well out of his depth.

phases.phase-4: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: three Medals of Honor and none of what Erskine was looking for. Handed the shield by committee, he takes the serum under pressure, and after losing his partner he executes a surrendering Flag Smasher with it in a public square, on camera. Stripped of the title, and picked up by Valentina as U.S. Agent before the episode is over.
phases.phase-6: Thunderbolts*: a mercenary with a failing marriage and a great deal to prove, thrown into Valentina's trap alongside people he would normally be fighting. The Void makes him look at his worst self, and he comes out something like a teammate.

characters.name: Gravik
characters.description: A young Skrull revolutionary leading a rogue faction that's done waiting for a new homeworld.

phases.phase-5: Secret Invasion: radicalised by thirty years of a promise Fury never kept, he runs the rebellion out of a repurposed reactor, with false-flag bombings, a Super-Skrull programme built from harvested Avengers DNA, and infiltrators as deep as War Machine. G'iah, powered by the same Harvest he was after, kills him in the finale.

characters.name: Parker Robbins / The Hood
characters.description: A charismatic Chicago crew leader who recruits Riri Williams for a string of high-tech heists, and whose gear works better than it has any right to.

phases.phase-5: Ironheart: he recruits Riri into his crew and offers her the funding the armour needs, and turns out to be powered by a cloak whose bargain runs on something a great deal older than technology. He offers her everything she says she wants, at a price she keeps agreeing to.

characters.name: Cassandra Nova
characters.description: A bald, terrifying telepath ruling a wasteland at the edge of existence.

phases.phase-4: Deadpool & Wolverine: Charles Xavier's twin sister, dumped in the Void as an infant and grown into the thing that runs it. A telepath who walks her fingers into people's skulls because she can. Wade and Logan's road trip goes straight through her court.

characters.name: Galactus
characters.description: A cosmic entity that devours entire worlds.

phases.phase-6: The Fantastic Four: First Steps: the Devourer of Worlds arrives at Earth-828 with one alternative to eating it, which is handing over the infant Franklin as a vessel for his hunger. The Four refuse, bait him across the planet, and put him through a teleport portal, and it costs Sue her life for as long as it takes Franklin to give it back.

characters.name: Ego
characters.description: Peter Quill's charming, mysterious, very long-lost father.

phases.phase-2: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2: a Celestial, and a living planet wearing a human body, who seeded children across the galaxy hoping one of them would be strong enough to power a second expansion. He killed every one that was not. He also put the tumour in Meredith Quill's head, and says so cheerfully. Peter stops being his battery, and the family blows him up from the core outwards.

characters.name: Ronan the Accuser
characters.description: A Kree fanatic wielding a war hammer and an apocalyptic grudge.

phases.phase-2: Guardians of the Galaxy: the zealot who breaks his deal with Thanos the moment the orb shows him what is inside it, and points planet-killing power at Xandar. He is undone by a dance-off and a held hand.
phases.phase-3: Captain Marvel: set in 1995, with a younger Ronan leading an Accuser bombardment of Earth until Carol takes his missiles, and most of his fleet, out of the sky on her own. He leaves saying they will be back for the weapon, meaning her.

characters.name: Ebony Maw
characters.description: A member of the Black Order gifted with telekinetic abilities and loyal servant to the mad Titan Thanos.

phases.phase-3:
Avengers: Infinity War: sent to Earth with Cull Obsidian to take the Time Stone, straight from the massacre of the Asgardians. He abducts Doctor Strange and tortures him to break the protective spells, and Iron Man blows him out of his own ship into vacuum.
Avengers: Endgame: the 2014 version comes forward with Thanos for the final battle.

characters.name: Cull Obsidian
characters.description: A member of the Black Order and loyal servant to the mad Titan Thanos.

phases.phase-3:
Avengers: Infinity War: sent with Ebony Maw to take the Time Stone, and driven off in New York by Iron Man, Doctor Strange, Wong and Spider-Man, losing an arm to a closing portal on the way. He is back at Wakanda with a prosthetic, where Banner kills him in the Hulkbuster armour.
Avengers: Endgame: the 2014 version is back for the final battle.

characters.name: The Collector
characters.description: A cosmic entity who collects rare and valuable items from across the universe.

phases.phase-2:
Thor: The Dark World: the post-credits. Asgard hands him the Aether for safekeeping, on the reasoning that two Infinity Stones in one vault is asking for trouble.
Guardians of the Galaxy: Taneleer Tivan, running a museum on Knowhere out of a hollowed-out celestial skull. He tries to buy the orb, and his assistant grabs the stone instead and takes most of the collection with her.
phases.phase-3: Avengers: Infinity War: Thanos takes Knowhere apart to get the Reality Stone, and what happens to Tivan is left unclear on screen. He survived it, and afterwards sold what was left of Knowhere to the Guardians.

characters.name: Georges Batroc / Batroc the Leaper
characters.description: A French mercenary and pirate for hire, quick enough on his feet to go hand to hand with a super soldier.

phases.phase-2: The Winter Soldier: hijacks the Lemurian Star with a crew of pirates and takes its engineers hostage, which is what puts Steve and Natasha on board in the first place. Steve goes at him hand to hand on deck and loses the mask doing it. Batroc ends the film in custody.
phases.phase-4: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: out again and running the hijacking Sam breaks up over Tunisia in the first episode, gone by parachute before Sam can get hold of him. Karli Morgenthau hires him with the Power Broker's own money for the fight in New York. He works out who has been paying him all along, tries to sell that back to her, and Sharon Carter shoots him for it.

characters.name: Arnim Zola
characters.description: The scientist who made Hydra work. Softly spoken, entirely without nerve, and considerably harder to be rid of than his employer.

phases.phase-1: Captain America: The First Avenger: Johann Schmidt's scientist, and the one who turns the Tesseract into something that can be fitted to a weapon. He runs the experiments on the prisoners at Krausberg, Bucky Barnes among them. Steve, Bucky and Gabe Jones take him off the Hydra train in the raid where Bucky falls, and Colonel Phillips works out during the interrogation that Zola is not carrying the cyanide pill every other Hydra agent has, which means he has no intention of dying for any of it. He tells them everything.
phases.phase-2: Captain America: The Winter Soldier: he never went to prison. The Americans brought him over under Operation Paperclip and put him to work, and he used the position to grow Hydra inside S.H.I.E.L.D. for decades. By 1972 he was dying, so his mind was copied onto banks of computers in a bunker in New Jersey, which is where Steve and Natasha find him. He explains what has been done to the agency, keeps them talking long enough for a missile to arrive, and the algorithm behind Project Insight is his.

characters.name: Abraham Erskine
characters.description: The scientist behind the super soldier serum, and the only person who ever knew the whole formula.

phases.phase-1: Captain America: The First Avenger: a German scientist who built the serum, watched Johann Schmidt take an unfinished version of it, and defected to the Americans afterwards. He chooses Steve Rogers over stronger candidates on the grounds that a weak man knows the value of strength, and he asks Steve to promise to stay who he is rather than become a perfect soldier. A Hydra assassin shoots him in the street hours after the procedure works. He had never written the formula down, and everything anyone tries afterwards is an attempt to rebuild what died with him.

characters.name: Obadiah Stane
characters.description: Howard Stark's old business partner, and the executive who kept Stark Industries running through all the years Tony was not paying attention to it.

phases.phase-1: Iron Man: he has run the company from just behind Tony's shoulder since Howard died, and he has been selling Stark weapons to both sides for years. The ambush in Afghanistan was a contract he took out on Tony, and when it fails he moves to take the company by having Tony declared unfit. He buys the wreck of the cave suit back off the Ten Rings, has the arc reactor pulled out of Tony's chest, and builds a far larger version of the armour for himself. Pepper Potts gets the evidence off his computer, and Stane dies over the Stark Industries building when Pepper overloads the arc reactor in the roof during the fight.

characters.name: Betty Ross
characters.description: A cellular biologist, Bruce Banner's partner in the work that went wrong, and General Ross's daughter.

phases.phase-1: The Incredible Hulk: she was working alongside Bruce on the gamma experiment and was badly hurt when it went wrong. Five years on she has rebuilt a life at Culver University and is seeing someone else, and she still holds the only surviving copy of the original data. She leaves with Bruce the moment he comes back for it, and puts herself between him and her father more than once.
phases.phase-6: Captain America: Brave New World: she is back in the story, with her father now President of the United States.

characters.name: Samuel Sterns
characters.description: A cellular biologist who spent years corresponding with Bruce Banner under the name Mr. Blue, and who wanted the gamma research for reasons of his own.

phases.phase-1: The Incredible Hulk: the scientist Bruce has been emailing as Mr. Blue, and the only person offering him a cure rather than a cage. He produces an antidote and it works. He has also quietly synthesised Banner's blood into a large stock of his own, which he intends to use on other things entirely. Emil Blonsky forces him to administer it, and in the struggle Sterns takes a head wound with that blood in it. The last shot of him is his skull starting to change shape.
phases.phase-6: Captain America: Brave New World: sixteen years later the film finally picks that up. Sterns is the Leader by now, and he has spent the intervening years in custody being used for what he can work out.

characters.name: Brock Rumlow / Crossbones
characters.description: A S.H.I.E.L.D. STRIKE team leader who works alongside Captain America, and who keeps turning up long after you would expect him to be finished.

phases.phase-2: Captain America: The Winter Soldier: leader of the STRIKE tactical team, working next to Steve Rogers on the Lemurian Star operation and then trying to kill him in a lift about twenty minutes later. He is Hydra, and has been the whole time. He fights Steve again at the Triskelion and is left badly burned when the helicarriers come down on top of him.
phases.phase-3:
Captain America: Civil War: back under the name Crossbones, masked because of the burns, robbing a biological weapons lab in Lagos. Steve stops him, and rather than be taken he sets off a vest. Wanda Maximoff throws the blast upward to save Steve and it takes out several floors of a building full of people, which is the incident the Sokovia Accords are written in response to.
Avengers: Endgame: he turns up again in the 2012 time heist, in the lift in the Triskelion, still a Hydra agent nobody has noticed yet. Steve gets past him without a fight.

characters.name: Ayesha
characters.description: High Priestess of the Sovereign, a gold-skinned people who grow their citizens to specification and consider themselves above everyone who does not.

phases.phase-2: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2: she hires the Guardians to defend the Sovereign's batteries from a monster, and Rocket steals some of the batteries on the way out. She sends a remotely piloted fleet after them for it, loses, and is humiliated in front of her own council for spending so much on a grudge. In the credits she stands in front of a birthing pod holding something she has grown specifically to destroy them, and names him Adam.
phases.phase-5: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3: still carrying the same grudge, and now working for the High Evolutionary, who created the Sovereign in the first place and treats Ayesha as a failed experiment. She sends Adam Warlock after Rocket before he is ready, which is most of why the film happens. By the end she dies protecting Adam from the Evolutionary.

characters.name: S.H.I.E.L.D.
characters.description: Strategic Homeland Intervention, Enforcement and Logistics Division. The international security agency that spent decades quietly cleaning up after the extraordinary, then decided to recruit it instead.

phases.phase-1:
Captain America: The First Avenger: not S.H.I.E.L.D. yet. The Strategic Scientific Reserve is the wartime outfit that runs Project Rebirth, and Peggy Carter and Howard Stark are the two people from it who go on to found the agency.
Iron Man: Agent Coulson spends the film trying to get a meeting, and the post-credits scene is Fury in Tony Stark's living room talking about the Avengers Initiative.
Iron Man 2: they bench Tony, and Natalie Rushman from legal turns out to have been a S.H.I.E.L.D. plant the whole time.
Thor: they seal off the crater in New Mexico, confiscate Jane Foster's research, and the post-credits scene has Erik Selvig handed the Tesseract to study.
The Avengers: the agency at its peak, with a flying helicarrier and the authority to pull six people into one room, and a World Security Council sitting above Fury telling him to put a nuclear missile into New York.
phases.phase-2:
Captain America: The Winter Soldier: HYDRA has been growing inside S.H.I.E.L.D. since the 1940s, in the machine Peggy and Howard built. Project Insight is what it was all for, three helicarriers set to kill everyone an algorithm flagged, and Steve Rogers brings the entire agency down rather than let them launch.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: what is left of it afterwards. Fury turns up at Clint Barton's farm with no organisation behind him, and still produces a helicarrier for the Sokovia evacuation.
phases.phase-3:
Ant-Man: the 1989 opening is a S.H.I.E.L.D. scene. Hank Pym resigns at the Triskelion in front of Peggy Carter and Howard Stark after finding out they have been trying to replicate his particle behind his back.
Captain Marvel: set in 1995, when it is a much smaller outfit and both Fury and Coulson are junior agents. Fury names the Avengers Initiative at the end of it, after Carol Danvers' call sign.
Avengers: Endgame: the time heist sends Steve back into the 2012 Triskelion, where he walks past his own body and talks a lift full of agents into handing over the sceptre.
phases.phase-4: Spider-Man: Far From Home: Peter Parker is recruited by what looks like a S.H.I.E.L.D. operation, with Fury and Maria Hill running him around Europe. Neither of them is who they appear to be, and the agency they seem to represent came apart years earlier.
phases.phase-5: Secret Invasion: the promise the whole series turns on was made by S.H.I.E.L.D. In 1995 Fury told Talos he would find the displaced Skrulls a home, and thirty years later he has not. The agency itself is long gone, and the response to the infiltration runs through Rhodey at the White House and Sonya Falsworth at MI6 instead.

characters.name: HYDRA
characters.description: Founded as the deep science division of the Nazi war machine, and considerably harder to kill than the regime it served.

phases.phase-1: Captain America: The First Avenger: Johann Schmidt runs it as Hitler's science division and then breaks from the Reich entirely, powering an arsenal with the Tesseract and building a bomber meant for American cities. Arnim Zola is the scientist making the weapons work, and he is taken alive when the war ends.
phases.phase-2:
Captain America: The Winter Soldier: Zola's deal after the war was Operation Paperclip, and he used it to grow HYDRA inside S.H.I.E.L.D. for seventy years. Alexander Pierce is running it from the top of the agency, Project Insight is the payoff, and the Winter Soldier is the asset they have been thawing out for jobs since the 1950s.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: Baron Strucker holds out in a Sokovian fortress with Loki's sceptre, and the experiments he runs on volunteers there are where Wanda and Pietro Maximoff get their powers.
phases.phase-3:
Ant-Man: Darren Cross sells the Yellowjacket suit to HYDRA, and Mitchell Carson walks out of the building with a vial of the shrinking particle.
Captain America: Civil War: the Siberian facility where five more Winter Soldiers were made, and the 1991 tape Zemo uses to take the Avengers apart.
Avengers: Endgame: Steve walks into the 2012 Triskelion and talks a lift full of HYDRA agents into handing him the sceptre without a fight.

characters.name: The Avengers
characters.description: The response team Nick Fury proposed when it became clear the world had started producing problems no single agency could handle.

phases.phase-1:
Iron Man: the post-credits scene is the first anyone hears of the Avengers Initiative, with Fury waiting in Tony Stark's living room.
Iron Man 2: Natasha Romanoff's assessment recommends Iron Man as a consultant and Tony Stark not at all.
The Avengers: six people who cannot stand each other are put in one room over the Tesseract, and by the end of it they are holding a street in Manhattan against an alien army.
phases.phase-2: Avengers: Age of Ultron: an established unit by now, working out of Stark Tower and clearing HYDRA holdouts together. Tony Stark and Bruce Banner build Ultron without telling the others, Sokovia is the cost, and the film closes on a completely different roster at an upstate compound: Steve, Natasha, Rhodey, Sam, Wanda and Vision.
phases.phase-3:
Ant-Man: Sam Wilson is on the compound grounds when Scott Lang breaks in, and the mid-credits scene is Sam and Steve with a problem they cannot solve on their own.
Captain America: Civil War: the Sokovia Accords split the team in half over whether it should answer to anyone, and it ends with an airport fight, a prison barge and Steve leaving the shield on the floor.
Spider-Man: Homecoming: Peter Parker spends the whole film desperate to be one, and turns the offer down when it finally comes.
Avengers: Infinity War: two years of nobody speaking, and they lose anyway. Half of them are dust by the credits.
Avengers: Endgame: five years later the survivors run a time heist to undo it. Everyone comes back through the portals for the last fight, and the team loses Natasha and Tony to win it.
phases.phase-4:
Spider-Man: Far From Home: with Tony dead, Steve gone and Thor off-world, the question the film keeps asking is who is left to do the job, and Nick Fury behaves as though Peter Parker is the answer.
Hawkeye: Clint Barton is the one still on the ground, and New York has turned the Battle of New York into a Broadway musical he has to sit through.
phases.phase-5: The Marvels: the end-credits scene has Kamala Khan let herself into Kate Bishop's flat with a folder, telling her she is putting a team together.
phases.phase-6: Thunderbolts*: Valentina Allegra de Fontaine presents her squad of expendables to the public as the New Avengers, and Sam Wilson files for the copyright on the name.

characters.name: Wakanda
characters.description: An East African nation the rest of the world believes is poor farmland, sitting on the only significant vibranium deposit on Earth.

phases.phase-2: Avengers: Age of Ultron: Ulysses Klaue's ship-breaking yard off the African coast is where Ultron goes for vibranium, and Klaue has a Wakandan brand burned into his neck for stealing it in the first place. This is the first time the country is named.
phases.phase-3:
Captain America: Civil War: the Accords conference in Vienna is bombed, King T'Chaka is killed in the blast, and his son goes after the man he believes did it. Wakanda takes Bucky Barnes in at the end and puts him back under.
Black Panther: T'Challa comes home to be crowned, and Killmonger's claim to the throne is built on Wakanda having watched the world from behind a shield and done nothing about it. T'Challa opens the borders at the end.
Avengers: Infinity War: the shield comes down and the country fights in the open for the first time in its history, and loses.
Avengers: Endgame: the Wakandan army comes back through the portals for the last fight.
phases.phase-4: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: Ayo and the Dora Milaje arrive in Latvia for Helmut Zemo, and put John Walker on the floor when he gets in the way. Ayo is also the one who did the deprogramming that made Bucky usable again, and Wakanda built the arm he is using.
phases.phase-5: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: T'Challa dies before the film begins, and Ramonda holds the throne through a year of other nations trying to take vibranium by force. An American vibranium detector in the Atlantic brings Namor and Talokan to the surface, Ramonda is killed defending the country, and Shuri takes the mantle.

characters.name: Asgard
characters.description: Odin's realm and Thor's home, the ruling power among the Nine Realms and considerably older than anywhere else in the story.

phases.phase-1: Thor: a golden city with a throne, a weapons vault and a coronation that gets interrupted. Thor is banished for restarting a war with Jotunheim, Odin falls into the Odinsleep, and Loki takes the throne and finds out where he actually came from. Thor destroys the Bifrost to stop him, which leaves Asgard cut off from the other realms.
phases.phase-2: Thor: The Dark World: Malekith and the Dark Elves attack the city itself, the dungeons are broken open in the fighting, and Frigga is killed defending Jane Foster. The film ends with Loki on the throne wearing Odin's face.
phases.phase-3:
Thor: Ragnarok: Odin dies in Norway and his firstborn is released by it. Hela takes Asgard in an afternoon, and the murals in the palace turn out to have been painted over the conquests the realm was built on. Thor works out that Ragnarok itself is the only thing that will stop her, and Loki sets Surtur loose to burn the city down. Asgard leaves as a ship full of refugees.
Avengers: Infinity War: the opening scene is that ship, already boarded, with half the survivors dead on the floor before the title card.
Avengers: Endgame: the ones who got out settle in a Norwegian fishing village they call New Asgard. Thor spends five years there drinking, and hands the crown to Valkyrie before leaving with the Guardians.
phases.phase-5: Thor: Love and Thunder: New Asgard has become a tourist town with a gift shop, a stage show and Valkyrie doing paperwork as king. Gorr attacks it and takes the children of the village, which is what brings Thor back.

characters.name: Kamar-Taj
characters.description: A walled compound in Kathmandu where an order of sorcerers has been training and defending the world for centuries, unnoticed by almost everyone.

phases.phase-3:
Doctor Strange: Stephen Strange arrives broke and desperate after spending everything on his hands, and the Ancient One takes him in. He learns the sling ring and the mirror dimension there, and finds out the order maintains three Sanctums that keep the Earth sealed. Kaecilius and the zealots attack the compound after stealing pages from the Book of Cagliostro, and Mordo walks away at the end over what the Ancient One had been doing to stay alive.
Avengers: Endgame: the portals that bring everyone to the final battle are opened out of Kamar-Taj, with Wong leading the masters through.
phases.phase-4:
Spider-Man: No Way Home: Wong is Sorcerer Supreme by now, and he leaves for Kamar-Taj early on after telling Strange the spell is his own problem to deal with.
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness: Wong shows Strange the Darkhold there and explains what Wanda Maximoff has been reading. She then attacks the compound directly to get to America Chavez, and the masters lose badly.
phases.phase-5:
Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings: the mid-credits scene. Wong brings Shang-Chi and Katy Chen here to work out what the ten rings actually are, with Bruce Banner and Carol Danvers joining by holographic call, and the meeting ends with nobody able to say where the beacon the rings have started sending is going.
She-Hulk: Attorney at Law: Wong is living there by now, and the series treats Kamar-Taj as somewhere between a headquarters and a flat. He portals out of it to collect Emil Blonsky from prison, has The Sopranos spoiled for him by a drunk woman who falls through a portal into his room, and later lets Blonsky come and stay.

characters.name: Sanctum Sanctorum
characters.description: A townhouse at 177A Bleecker Street in New York, one of three Sanctums holding the Earth's defences shut, and Doctor Strange's address.

phases.phase-3:
Doctor Strange: the New York Sanctum is one of three, with London and Hong Kong, and together they maintain the shield around the Earth. Kaecilius kills the master of the New York Sanctum, Strange ends up defending it more or less by accident, and that is how he inherits it.
Thor: Ragnarok: Thor and Loki are held there while Strange establishes what they want, and Loki spends a good while falling through a portal for being difficult about it.
Avengers: Infinity War: Ebony Maw comes for the Time Stone, takes the building apart around Strange and Wong, and lifts Strange off the street outside it.
Avengers: Endgame: the time heist sends Bruce Banner back to the 2012 Sanctum, where he has to talk the Ancient One into handing over the Time Stone.
phases.phase-4:
Spider-Man: No Way Home: Peter Parker comes to Bleecker Street to ask for a spell that will make the world forget who he is. It is cast in the undercroft beneath the building, Peter talks over it while it is running, and most of the film follows from that.
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness: Strange is living there at the start, and America Chavez arrives in the street outside with something chasing her across universes. The Earth-838 version of the building has a statue of that universe's Strange standing outside it and Karl Mordo as its master, and Mordo greets the pair at the door, invites them in and drugs their tea.

characters.name: The Ten Rings
characters.description: A criminal organisation that turns up under several different guises long before the story gets round to explaining what it actually is.

phases.phase-1: Iron Man: the cell that ambushes Tony Stark's convoy in Afghanistan and holds him in a cave to build them a missile. Raza is the one giving orders on the ground, the weapons they are carrying are all Stark Industries stock, and the contract that put Tony in that cave was taken out by Obadiah Stane.
phases.phase-2: Iron Man 3: the Mandarin's broadcasts go out under the Ten Rings name and use its imagery, and the whole thing is staged. Trevor Slattery is an actor hired to read the speeches, and Aldrich Killian is using the campaign as cover for Extremis subjects failing in public.
phases.phase-5: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings: the real one. Xu Wenwu found the ten rings a thousand years ago and has run the organisation ever since, under a different name in every century. The outfit that took Tony Stark carries the same name and the same symbol, and Killian's fake Mandarin is an insult Wenwu takes personally enough to have Slattery abducted over it. The film ends with the rings on Shang-Chi's arms and the organisation handed to Xu Xialing, and the mid-credits scene has Wong take him to Kamar-Taj, where he, Bruce Banner and Carol Danvers all fail to say what the rings are or where the signal they have started sending is going.

characters.name: The Red Room
characters.description: A Soviet programme that took girls, trained them into assassins, and went on turning them out long after the Soviet Union stopped existing.

phases.phase-2: Avengers: Age of Ultron: Wanda Maximoff puts Natasha Romanoff through a vision of it, and that is the first the audience sees of the place. The ballet studio, the shooting drills, and the graduation ceremony at the end of the programme, which is a forced hysterectomy carried out so that nothing can ever compete with the work.
phases.phase-3: Black Widow: Dreykov is alive, and the Red Room has been moved into a facility that flies, kept in the air over Russia so that nobody can find it. Every Widow is sedated going in and out so none of them can say where it is. They are chemically controlled rather than simply trained, and Melina Vostokoff's antidote is the only thing that breaks it. Natasha, Yelena Belova, Melina and Alexei Shostakov bring the facility down between them, Dreykov dies in it, and the freed Widows scatter with enough antidote to reach the rest.
phases.phase-6: Thunderbolts*: the Red Room appears in flashback, in what Yelena Belova remembers of where she came from.

characters.name: The Quantum Realm
characters.description: A dimension sitting underneath our own, reached by shrinking past the point where the ordinary laws of physics stop applying.

phases.phase-3:
Doctor Strange: the Ancient One pushes Strange out of his body and throws him through a run of dimensions, and the Quantum Realm is one of the places he passes through.
Ant-Man: Hank Pym describes it as where you end up if you shrink too far, and says nobody comes back. Scott Lang goes subatomic to get through Darren Cross's suit and does come back, which is what makes Hank think Janet might still be alive down there.
Ant-Man and the Wasp: the whole film is an attempt to open a stable tunnel and get Janet van Dyne out after thirty years. It works. The post-credits scene then strands Scott in it when the Snap takes everyone standing at the controls.
Avengers: Endgame: five years for everyone else turn out to have been five hours for Scott, and that gap is what tells him the Quantum Realm can be used to move through time. The entire heist runs on it.
phases.phase-4: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania: the whole film happens down there, and the place turns out to be inhabited. There are cities, a ruling power and a resistance fighting it. Janet van Dyne spent decades in the middle of all of it and told nobody, including the part where she helped Kang the Conqueror repair his ship and then stranded him.

characters.name: The Department of Damage Control
characters.description: A federal agency set up to clear away what the fighting leaves behind, and steadily more interested in the people doing the fighting.

phases.phase-3: Spider-Man: Homecoming: a joint federal and Stark Industries operation formed to clean up after the Battle of New York, and the reason Adrian Toomes loses the salvage contract that was keeping his crew in work. Anne Marie Hoag runs it. Peter Parker also spends thirty-seven minutes locked in one of their storage vaults, which is where he works out what his suit can actually do.
phases.phase-4: Spider-Man: No Way Home: they arrest Peter, MJ, Ned and May in the first few minutes and hold them for questioning over Mysterio's broadcast, with Agent Cleary running the interviews.
phases.phase-5: Ms. Marvel: by this point it hunts enhanced people as a matter of policy rather than cleaning up after them. Agent Deever runs the Jersey City operation against Kamala Khan, using Stark drones and a sonic cannon in an alleyway and later raiding her school. Cleary is the one above her, and he is the same official who handled Peter Parker.

characters.name: Knowhere
characters.description: A mining colony built inside the severed head of a dead Celestial, floating at the edge of everything and run with no law worth the name.

phases.phase-2:
Thor: The Dark World: the mid-credits scene is Sif and Volstagg handing the Aether to the Collector, who keeps his collection here.
Guardians of the Galaxy: the Guardians bring the Orb to the Collector to sell it. He explains what the Infinity Stones are and where they came from, and then one of his slaves grabs the thing and takes out most of the museum with it.
phases.phase-3: Avengers: Infinity War: Thanos gets there first. The museum is already burning by the time the Guardians arrive, he has the Reality Stone before any of them work out what they are looking at, and he takes Gamora with him when he goes.
phases.phase-5:
The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special: the Guardians have bought Knowhere from the Collector and are living in it, and Mantis and Drax leave it for Earth to fetch Kevin Bacon as a Christmas present for Quill.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3: home and headquarters for the whole film. Adam Warlock attacks it in the opening and very nearly kills Rocket, and by the end it is full of the children taken off the High Evolutionary's ship, with Rocket in charge of the place.

characters.name: The TVA
characters.description: The Time Variance Authority. An organisation sitting outside time that arrests people for departing from the one approved version of history, and does not take questions about who approved it.

phases.phase-4:
Loki: Season 1: an agency outside time, staffed by people who believe three Time-Keepers created them, and empowered to delete anyone whose life departs from the Sacred Timeline. Loki is taken the moment he picks up the Tesseract in 2012, and Mobius recruits him rather than prune him. The Time-Keepers turn out to be animatronic props, every analyst and hunter turns out to be an abducted variant with their memory wiped, and the person actually running it has been sitting alone at the end of time the whole while.
Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania: the post-credits scene is Loki and Mobius in a theatre, watching Victor Timely give a lecture.
Loki: Season 2: the Temporal Loom is failing, because the branching it was built to stop is now happening faster than it can be pruned. Miss Minutes turns out to have intentions of her own, Ravonna Renslayer throws in with Timely, and Loki spends the season learning to control his time-slipping well enough to do something about it. He ends up holding the branches open himself, in place of the Loom.
Deadpool & Wolverine: Mr. Paradox runs a TVA branch with an unauthorised Time Ripper installed, and his answer to a universe whose Anchor Being has died is to speed its collapse up rather than wait. He prunes Wade Wilson into the Void when Wade will not go along with it.

characters.name: The Void
characters.description: The place at the end of time where the TVA dumps everything it prunes, with something living there that makes sure none of it comes back.

phases.phase-4:
Loki: Season 1: where Loki wakes up after being pruned, in the ruins of a New York that stops at a wall of nothing. What the TVA deletes is not destroyed, it is dropped here, and Alioth is the thing that keeps it here. Loki finds four other versions of himself surviving in it, and the way out runs past Alioth to the Citadel at the End of Time.
Deadpool & Wolverine: Mr. Paradox prunes Wade Wilson and Logan into it. By now it has a society, run by Cassandra Nova out of the remains of the people and places that other timelines lost, and Alioth is still outside the walls.

characters.name: Talokan
characters.description: An underwater kingdom off the Yucatán coast, hidden for four and a half centuries, and the only place on Earth besides Wakanda with vibranium.

phases.phase-5: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: founded in 1571, when a Yucatán Mayan village dying of smallpox took a herb grown from a vibranium meteor on the sea floor and became something that could breathe water. Namor was born during that change, aged differently from everyone else, and has ruled since. When an American vibranium detector starts working the Atlantic, Talokan reads it as the beginning of the same thing the Spanish did to them, and Namor comes to Wakanda to say the two nations can either take the surface world on together or fight each other first. They fight each other first.

characters.name: Vormir
characters.description: A dead planet at the far edge of space, with a mountain at its centre and a single very old inhabitant.

phases.phase-3:
Avengers: Infinity War: Thanos brings Gamora here for the Soul Stone. The keeper waiting at the top is the Red Skull, moved here by the Tesseract at the end of Captain America: The First Avenger and left to guard a stone he is not permitted to touch. The stone will only be given up in exchange for someone the taker loves, so Thanos throws Gamora off the cliff.
Avengers: Endgame: Natasha Romanoff and Clint Barton arrive for the same stone under the same terms, and spend the scene fighting each other over which of them goes over the edge. Natasha is the one who does.
phases.phase-4: Hawkeye: Vormir turns up in Clint Barton's flashbacks, in what he keeps going back to about how Natasha died.

characters.name: Stark Industries
characters.description: The manufacturer Howard Stark founded and his son inherited, which walked out of the weapons business overnight and spent the following decade building something else.

phases.phase-1:
Captain America: The First Avenger: Howard Stark runs it through the war, and he is the one who builds the vibranium shield and the machinery that turns Steve Rogers into a super-soldier.
Iron Man: the largest weapons manufacturer in the country, with Obadiah Stane on the board selling to both sides of the war Tony is demonstrating missiles in. Tony shuts the weapons division down at a press conference the week he gets home, and the share price falls through the floor.
Iron Man 2: Tony signs the company over to Pepper Potts and puts on the Stark Expo, while Justin Hammer chases the military contracts Stark walked away from and cannot build anything that works.
The Avengers: Stark Tower goes up in Manhattan running on its own arc reactor, and it is the roof Loki opens the portal from.
phases.phase-2:
Iron Man 3: barely a company in this one. Aldrich Killian pitches Advanced Idea Mechanics as the thing Stark Industries used to be, and Tony spends the middle of the film with no resources beyond what he can build in a shed in Tennessee.
Avengers: Age of Ultron: Stark Tower becomes Avengers Tower, and the company's upstate facility becomes the team's base by the end of it.
phases.phase-3:
Captain America: Civil War: Tony opens the film funding an entire MIT graduating class, and the woman who stops him in the corridor afterwards to talk about her son in Sokovia is why he signs the Accords.
Spider-Man: Homecoming: a Stark internship is Peter Parker's cover story, Happy Hogan is running the move of everything out of Avengers Tower to the upstate compound, and the truck Toomes' crew goes after is carrying Stark property.
phases.phase-4: Spider-Man: Far From Home: EDITH is a Stark Industries system left to Peter in Tony's will, with command of the company's satellites and a drone fleet. Quentin Beck used to work there and was fired, and the crew helping him fake the Elementals is made up of other people the company got rid of.

characters.name: S.W.O.R.D.
characters.description: The Sentient Weapon Observation and Response Division, founded by Maria Rambeau to keep watch on whatever comes at Earth from space.

phases.phase-4: WandaVision: Maria Rambeau built it after 1995 for manned missions and extraterrestrial contact, and Tyler Hayward has since turned it toward robotics, artificial intelligence and weapons instead. S.W.O.R.D. is the operation that sets up outside Westview, establishes that Wanda Maximoff is generating the anomaly, and sends Monica Rambeau in through it. Hayward has also been quietly rebuilding Vision's body out of the remains he took, a programme he calls Cataract, and he launches it at Wanda while telling everyone the operation is a rescue.

characters.name: The Skrulls
characters.description: A species that can take the shape of anyone they have seen, scattered across the galaxy after losing a war, and looking for somewhere to live.

phases.phase-3: Captain Marvel: introduced as the enemy, shapeshifting infiltrators the Kree have been hunting for decades. Carol Danvers works out partway through that she has been fighting for the wrong side, and that Talos and the group on Earth are refugees trying to find Mar-Vell's engine so they can leave. Fury promises to help them find a home, and Carol goes off to look for one.
phases.phase-4:
WandaVision: the mid-credits scene is a Skrull inside the FBI approaching Monica Rambeau to say an old friend of her mother's wants to see her.
Spider-Man: Far From Home: Talos and his wife Soren spend the entire film standing in for Nick Fury and Maria Hill, running Peter Parker around Europe, while the real Fury is on a station in orbit.
phases.phase-5:
Secret Invasion: after the Snap, Talos called every scattered Skrull he could reach to Earth, and thirty years on Fury still has not found them anywhere else to go. A faction under Gravik stops waiting and starts replacing people in governments, aiming to start a war big enough to leave the planet empty. Gravik kills Talos, Rhodey turns out to have been replaced some time ago, and it ends with the President signing an order that makes every Skrull on Earth a target.
The Marvels: Dar-Benn strips Tarnax, the refugee colony that never made it to Earth, of what was keeping it liveable, as one of the raids she runs to keep Hala going.

characters.name: The Kree Empire
characters.description: A galactic empire ruled from Hala by an artificial intelligence, and a very long way into a war with the Skrulls.

phases.phase-2: Guardians of the Galaxy: the empire has signed a peace treaty with Xandar and Ronan the Accuser refuses to honour it. He takes the Orb meaning to use it on Xandar himself, and Korath works for him until the Guardians get in the way.
phases.phase-3: Captain Marvel: most of the film happens inside it. Hala is the capital, the Supreme Intelligence is the artificial intelligence running the empire and it appears to every Kree as the person they most admire, and Starforce is its elite unit. Carol Danvers has been serving in it for six years believing she is Kree. The war against the Skrulls turns out to be an extermination campaign, and Carol burns the Accusers' fleet on her way out.
phases.phase-5: The Marvels: Hala is dying. The sun is failing, the air is going, and the civil war that followed Carol destroying the Supreme Intelligence has left the place wrecked. Dar-Benn holds Carol responsible for all of it and uses a Quantum Band to tear resources out of other worlds to keep Hala breathing. Carol ends the film by restoring the sun.

characters.name: The Celestials
characters.description: Enormous beings that predate almost everything else, and have been seeding and harvesting inhabited worlds for longer than any civilisation in the story has existed.

phases.phase-2:
Guardians of the Galaxy: the Collector's account of where the Infinity Stones came from includes a Celestial called Eson using the Power Stone to strip a populated planet down to bare rock. Knowhere is a Celestial too, or what is left of one, mined for whatever is still inside the skull.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2: Ego describes himself as one. A consciousness that woke up alone and grew a planet around itself, and the seedlings he has planted on thousands of worlds are meant to convert all of them into more of him.
phases.phase-5: Eternals: the film that explains what they are for. Arishem the Judge seeds inhabited worlds with a Celestial waiting to hatch, and sends Eternals ahead to protect the population until there are enough of them to power the birth, which destroys the planet. Earth is carrying Tiamut. The Eternals stop the Emergence between them, and Arishem takes several of them away to decide whether humanity gets to continue.
phases.phase-6: Captain America: Brave New World: Tiamut's body is still in the Indian Ocean where it stopped, and the island that has formed around it is full of adamantium. Most of the film is governments manoeuvring over who gets to mine it.

characters.name: The Ravagers
characters.description: An interstellar syndicate of thieves, smugglers and pirates, split into roughly a hundred clans, each with its own captain and its own opinion of the others.

phases.phase-2:
Guardians of the Galaxy: Yondu Udonta's clan collected Peter Quill off Earth as a child and kept him. Quill then steals the Orb out from under a job the clan was hired for, and they hunt him for most of the film until he trades it back in exchange for their help against Ronan over Xandar.
Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2: the code and the politics behind it. Stakar Ogord freed Yondu from Kree slavery and gave him a clan, then exiled him for trafficking children, which is what Yondu was doing the day he picked up Quill. Taserface leads a mutiny and most of the clan dies in it. Yondu dies getting Quill out of Ego, and Stakar gives him the Ravager funeral he had been denied, with all the old captains turning up for it.
phases.phase-5: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3: Stakar's United Ravagers, a coalition of clans put together after the Blip, help the Guardians get into the Orgoscope. The Gamora in this film is one of them, having been taken in by Stakar's clan after Endgame left her stranded outside her own timeline.

characters.name: Mutants
characters.description: People born carrying a gene nobody gave them, which activates somewhere in the course of their lives and leaves them with abilities or a changed body.

phases.phase-4:
Deadpool & Wolverine: most of the Void's population turns out to be mutant. Laura, Elektra, Gambit and Blade are all down there, put there by the TVA, and Cassandra Nova running the place is Charles Xavier's twin sister.
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness: Charles Xavier sits on the Illuminati of Earth-838 as that universe's representative for mutants.
phases.phase-5:
Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: Namor uses the word about himself, which is the first time anyone in the main timeline does.
Ms. Marvel: Bruno tells Kamala that her genes carry a mutation the rest of her family does not have, and the X-Men theme plays underneath the line.
The Marvels: the post-credits scene puts Monica Rambeau in a universe that is not hers, with Beast standing over her.

characters.name: Sakaar
characters.description: A rubbish planet at the far end of a cluster of wormholes, where anything lost in the universe eventually washes up, run as an arena by the Grandmaster.

phases.phase-3: Thor: Ragnarok: Thor lands here after Hela throws him off the Bifrost, and is collected as scrap. The Grandmaster runs the planet and the Contest of Champions in it, and his reigning champion is the Hulk, who flew off in the Quinjet at the end of Age of Ultron and has not turned back into Bruce Banner in the two years since. Valkyrie is here as well, drinking, working as a scrapper since Hela wiped out the Valkyries. Thor gets all three of them off the planet, and Korg's revolution takes over what is left.
phases.phase-5: She-Hulk: Attorney at Law: Bruce Banner leaves Earth on a Sakaaran ship partway through the series and comes back with a son. Skaar was born on Sakaar, and time runs differently enough there that he is a teenager by the time Bruce brings him to a family barbecue in Los Angeles.

characters.name: CIA
characters.description: The United States' foreign intelligence service. Everett Ross has worked for it since well before anyone in Wakanda met him.

phases.phase-3: Black Panther: Everett Ross is the agency's man on Ulysses Klaue, which is why he is in the casino in Busan when T'Challa arrives for the same target. He takes a bullet meant for Nakia, is patched up in Wakanda with technology nobody outside it has, and flies a Talon remotely for them at the end. Killmonger's ghost unit had also worked with the CIA destabilising foreign governments, and that is where he learned the method he brings home with him.
phases.phase-5: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever: Valentina Allegra de Fontaine is Director by now, with Ross working under her and quietly passing Shuri and Okoye everything he sees. The vibranium detector that sets the whole crisis off is an American project. Val has Ross arrested for the leaks at the end of it.
phases.phase-6: Thunderbolts*: Val is still Director and facing impeachment over the black projects she has been running off the books, and the squad she puts together is meant to destroy the evidence of them for her.

characters.name: Earth-616
characters.description: The universe the whole story takes place in, and the designation it acquires once other universes start arriving in it.

phases.phase-4:
Spider-Man: Far From Home: Quentin Beck introduces the number. He claims to be from Earth-833 and calls this one Earth-616, as part of a multiverse story he has invented from nothing to sell a threat that does not exist.
Spider-Man: No Way Home: the first real crossing. Strange's spell pulls in everyone from other universes who knew Peter Parker's identity, and it ends with Peter erased from the memory of every person in his own.
Deadpool & Wolverine: the universe the Deadpool and X-Men films take place in is designated Earth-10005, and the TVA's working rule is that a universe begins to die when its Anchor Being does.
Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness: Earth-838 is named and visited, the Christine Palmer there uses both numbers out loud, and an incursion is defined as what happens when two universes are pushed into each other.

characters.name: Madripoor
characters.description: A city-state in Southeast Asia divided between Hightown and Lowtown, with a smuggling port and no extradition treaty with anyone.

phases.phase-4: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: Sam Wilson, Bucky Barnes and Helmut Zemo go there to find whoever recreated the super soldier serum. Getting through Lowtown means Bucky playing the Winter Soldier again in front of people who remember him as one. Sharon Carter has been living there since going on the run after Civil War, and the Power Broker everyone in the city is frightened of turns out to be her.

characters.name: S.A.B.E.R.
characters.description: Strategic Aerospace Biophysics and Exolinguistic Response. The aerospace defence operation Nick Fury was sent to build after the Blip, run off a station in orbit and staffed by humans and Skrulls together.

phases.phase-4: WandaVision: the mid-credits scene is a Skrull inside the FBI approaching Monica Rambeau on Fury's behalf, recruiting her for S.A.B.E.R. and for an assignment that is not on this planet.
phases.phase-5:
Secret Invasion: Fury comes down from the station at the start of the series and goes back up at the end of it with Varra, having agreed to try opening talks between the Skrulls and the Kree.
The Marvels: the station is where most of the film is coordinated from. Fury runs it, Kamala Khan's family end up aboard, and when Dar-Benn's damage reaches it the evacuation is carried out by Goose and a very large number of flerken kittens swallowing everyone on board.

characters.name: New Avengers
characters.description: A team announced as Avengers some years after Endgame, by a government that wanted one of its own.

phases.phase-6:
Thunderbolts*: Valentina Allegra de Fontaine already had a press conference booked by the time the fighting in New York stopped, and she used it to present the group as a team she had been assembling all along. Yelena Belova, Bucky Barnes, Alexei Shostakov, Ava Starr and John Walker walk out on stage and go along with it, and Yelena tells Val to her face that they own her now. They take the Watchtower as a headquarters and get matching uniforms and a place on a cereal box, and Bob Reynolds stays with them without going out on the work.
Fourteen months later Sam Wilson is assembling an Avengers team of his own and has filed for the copyright on the name, which leaves this one arguing about which of them counts as the real thing while a ship nobody recognises comes down over the city.
